Lod, Ono and in the Zimmer Valley.
And certain of the Levites, which had part in Judah, dwelt among Benjamin.
These are the priests and the Levites that went up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua; Seraiah; Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattus,
Sechanja, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Ginthoi, Abia,
Mejamin, Maadja, Bilga,
Shemaiah, Jehoiarib, Jedaiah,
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. These were the chief among the priests and their brethren in the days of Jesus.
And the Levites were these: Jeshua, Benui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mathaniah, about the thanksgiving, he and his brethren.
Bakbukiah and Unni, her brethren, were on guard for her.
Jeshua begat Jehoiakim, Jehoiakim begat Eliasib, Eliasib begat Jehoiada.
Jehoiada begat Jonathan, Jonathan begat Jaddua.
And in the days of Jehoiakim these were chief fathers among the priests: namely, of Seraiah was Meraiah; of Jeremiah was Hananiah;.
Of Ezra was Meshullam; of Amariah was Johanan;
Of Malluch was Jonathan; of Zebaniah was Joseph;
Of Harim was Adnah; of Meraioth was Helkai;
Of Iddo was Zechariah; of Ginthon was Meshullam.
Of Abijah was Zichri; of Mejamin-moyah was Piltai;
Of Bilgah was Shammua; of Shemaiah was Jonathan;
Of Jehoiarib was Mathnai; of Jedaiah was Uzzi;
From Sallai was Kallai; from Amok was Eber;
Of Hilkiah was Hashabiah; of Jedaiah was Nethaneel.
And in the days of Eliasib, and Jehoiada, and Johanan, and Jaddua, the chief fathers among the Levites, and the priests, were described under the kingdom of Darii the Persian.
And the children of Levi, the chief fathers, were written in the book of the chronicles unto the days of Johanan the son of Eliasib.

And these were the chief of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, and their brethren beside them, to praise and to give thanks, as David the man of God commanded, one hat for another.
And Mathaniah, and Bakbukiah, and Obadiah, and Meshulam, and Talmon, and Akub, were keepers of the guard, at the thresholds of the gates.
These were in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and Ezra the priest the scribe.

And in the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem they sought the Levites out of all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem, to keep the dedication with gladness, with singing, and cymbals, and psalteries, and harps.
And there were gathered together the children of the singers, and from the coasts of Jerusalem, and from the courts of Netophathi.
And of the house of Gilgal, and of the fields of Gibeah, and of Azmaveth: for the singers had built them courts round about Jerusalem.
And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and cleansed the people, and the gates, and the wall.
And I set the princes of Judah upon the top of the wall, and appointed two great choirs of thanksgiving, which went up on the right hand upon the top of the wall toward the dung gate.
And unto them went Hoshaiah, and half the princes of Judah.
and Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah and Jeremiah
And some of the sons of the priests with trumpets; Zechariah the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mathaniah, the son of Michaiah, the son of Zechur, the son of Asaph,
And his brethren, Shemaiah, and Azareel, and Milalai, and Gilalai, and Maai, and Nethaneel, and Judah, Hanani, with the stringed instruments of David the man of God: and Ezra the scribe before them,
And they went toward the well gate. And they walked beside them in the steps of the city of David, up the wall unto the house of David, unto the water gate eastward.
And the other choir of thanksgiving went over against them, and I after them, and half the people up the wall unto the tower of the furnace, unto the broad wall,
And they went up to the gate of Ephraim, and to the old gate, and to the fish gate, and to the tower of Hananeel, and to the tower of Mea, unto the sheep gate, and stood in the prison gate.
And the two thanksgivings were in the house of God, and I and half of the princes with me;
And the priests, namely, Eliakim, Maeshiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, Hananiah, with trumpets;

And Maeshiah, and Shemaiah, and Eleazar, and Uzzi, and Johanan, and Malchiah, and Elam, and Azar. And the singers sang aloud; and Jezrahiah was the ruler. 43; And they offered great sacrifices that day, and were glad: for God had made them great joy, that both wives and children rejoiced: and the joy of Jerusalem was heard afar off.

At that time were men appointed over the treasuries, when the heaves, and the firstfruits, and the tithes, were in, to gather them out of the fields, and round about the cities, to distribute according to the law unto the priests and to the Levites: for Judah delighted in the priests and the Levites, that they should tarry
And they waited upon the guard of their God, and upon the guard of purification. And the singers and the porters kept the charge of David, and of Solomon his son.
For in the days of David and Assaph were established the chief singers, and singers of praise and thanksgiving unto GOD.

And all Israel gave portions unto the singers and unto the porters in the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, every day his portion: and they gave sanctuaries unto the Levites, and the Levites gave sanctuaries unto the children of Aaron.
And the book of Moses was read in that day in the ears of the people, and it was found written therein, that the Ammonites and the Moabites should no more come into the congregation of God,
Because they prevented not the children of Israel with bread and water, and set Balaam against them to curse them: but our God turned the curse into a blessing.
And when they heard this law, they separated all the strangers from Israel.
And before him Eliasib the priest had put Tobiah's offering in the treasury of the house of our God.

For he had made him a great coffer, and therein they had laid the meat offering, and the incense, and the vessels, and the tithes of the corn, and the wine, and the oil, according to the commandment of the Levites, and the singers, and the porters, and the heaves of the priests.
But in all this I was not at Jerusalem. For in the thirty-second year of Arthahaztha king of Babylon I came to the king, and after some days I purchased of the king,
And I went to Jerusalem. And I perceived that it was not good which Eliasib had done to Tobiah, to make him a box in the court of the house of God.
And I was sore displeased, and cast out all the vessels of the house of Tobiah from before the box.
And I commanded that they should cleanse the caskets: and I brought again there the vessels of the house of God, the meat offering, and the incense.
And I heard that the Levites' portion was not given unto them, because the Levites and the singers fled every man to his field to work.
And I rebuked the princes, saying, Why do we forsake the house of God? But I gathered them together, and set them in their place.
And all Judah brought tithes of the corn, and of the wine, and of the oil, unto the treasury.

And I set over the treasures Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites Pedaiah, and under their hand Hanan the son of Zechur the son of Mathaniah: for they were counted faithful, and were commanded to distribute unto their brethren.
Remember me, O my God, and do not blot out my mercy, which I have done to my God's house and to his guard.

At that time I saw winepresses treading in Judah on the sabbath day, and bringing in sheaves, and asses laden with wine, and with grapes, and with figs, and with all manner of burden, to Jerusalem on the sabbath day. I saw them on the day they sold the food.
There dwelt also Tyrians within, which brought fishes and all manner of merchandise, and sold them on the sabbath day unto the children of Judah and Jerusalem.
Then I rebuked the princes of Judah, and said unto them: What wicked thing is this that ye do, and break the sabbath day?
Did not our fathers do so, and our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city? And ye make more wrath upon Israel, because ye break the sabbath day.

And when the gates of Jerusalem were opened before the sabbath day, I commanded the doors to be shut, and commanded that they should not be opened until after the sabbath day. And I appointed some of my servants to the gates, that no burden should be brought in on the sabbath day.
And the merchants and the sellers, with all manner of merchandise, stayed out of Jerusalem one night or two.
Then I testified unto them, and said unto them: Why tarry ye about the wall overnight? If ye do it again, I will lay hands on you. From that time forth they came not on the sabbath day.
And I spake unto the Levites that were clean, that they should come and keep the gates, to hallow the sabbath day. O my God, remember me also, and spare me according to thy great mercy.
I saw also in those days Jews taking wives of Ashdod, and Ammon, and Moab.
And their children spake half of them asdodish, and could not speak Jewish, but after the manner of every people.

And I reproached them, and cursed them, and smote certain men, and roughed them up, and took an oath of them by God, saying, Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, neither shall ye take their daughters unto your sons, or unto yourselves.

Did not Solomon king of Israel sin in this? And yet in many nations there was no king like unto him, and he was dear unto his God, and God made him king over all Israel: nevertheless the foreign wives made him to sin.
Have ye not heard that ye do such great evil, to trespass against our God, and to take foreign wives?
And one of the sons of Jehoiada the son of Eliasib the high priest had made friends with Sanballat the Horonite: but I put him away from me.
Remember them, O my God, that are loosed from the priesthood, and from the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.
So I cleansed them from all foreigners, and set the guard of the priests and Levites, every man according to his business,
And to offer the wood at appointed times, and the firstfruits. Remember me, my God, in the best!
In the days of Ahasuerus, which was king from India unto the Moors, over an hundred and twenty and seven countries,
And as he sat in his royal seat in Shushan the palace,
In the third year of his reign he made a feast with him unto all his princes and servants, even to the mighty men of Persia and Media, and to the governors and princes of his provinces,
That he might shew the marvellous riches of his kingdom, and the glorious majesty of his majesty, for many days, even an hundred and fourscore days.
And when the days were expired, the king made a feast unto all the people that were in Shushan the palace, both great and small, seven days in the court of the garden of the king's house.

There hung white, red, and yellow cloths, bound with linen and scarlet ropes in silver rings upon marble pillars. The benches were of gold and silver, made upon pavements of green, white, yellow, and black marbles.
And the drink was carried in vessels of gold, and other vessels, and other vessels, and royal wine in such quantity as the king was able.
And they appointed no man what he should drink: for the king had commanded all the rulers of his house that every man should do as he pleased.
And Vasthi the queen also made a feast for the women in the royal house of king Ahasuerus,
And on the seventh day, when the king was well pleased with wine, he called Mehuman, Bistha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Sethar, and Kharkas, the seven eunuchs that ministered before king Ahasuerus,
And they brought Vashti the queen before the king with the royal crown, to shew her beauty unto the people and to the princes: for she was fair.
But Vasthi the queen would not come after the king's word by his chamberlains. And the king was very wroth, and his wrath was kindled in him.
And the king spake unto the wise men that had knowledge of the customs of the land, (for the king's things must be done in the sight of all that have understanding of right and wrong;

And the next unto him were Charsena, and Sethar, and Admatha, and Tharsis, and Meres, and Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of the Persians and Medes, which saw the king's face, and sat on high in the kingdom),
What right should be done to Vasthi the queen, because she had not done according to the king's word by his chamberlains?

And Memucan said before the king and princes, Vashti the queen hath not wrought evil against the king only, but also against all the princes, and against all the people of all the provinces of king Ahasuerus.

For such a deed shall come forth from the queen unto all the women, that they shall despise their husbands in their sight, and shall say, Ahasuerus the king called Vashti the queen to come before him; but she would not.
Now therefore the princesses of Persia and Media shall say so also unto all the king's princes, when they hear such a deed of the queen; and there shall be enough contempt and wrath.

If it please the king, let a royal decree go forth from him, and let it be written according to the law of the Persians and Medes, which shall not be transgressed, that Vashti come no more before king Ahasuerus; and let the king give her kingdom to her neighbour that is better than she;
And that this letter of the king's, which is made, may go forth into all his kingdom (which is great), that all the women may keep their husbands in honour, both great and small.
And it pleased the king and the princes: and the king did according to the word of Memucan.

And letters were sent into all the king's provinces, into every land according to the writing thereof, and unto every people according to their language, that every man should be ruler in his house, and speak according to the language of his people.
After these things, when the wrath of king Ahasuerus was abated, he remembered Vasthi, what she had done, and what was decreed concerning her.
Then said the king's lads that ministered unto him: Let young virgins be sought for the king;

And the king shall appoint showers throughout all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather together all manner of fair young virgins unto Shushan the palace, into the women's chamber, under the hand of Hegai the king's chamberlain, who waiteth upon the women, and give them their jewels;
And whichever damsel pleaseth the king, let her be queen in Vashti's stead. And this pleased the king, and he did so.
Now there was a certain Jew in Shushan the palace, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, the son of Jemini,
Who was carried away with him from Jerusalem, when Jechaniah king of Judah was carried away, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon carried away.

And he was a guardian to Hadassah, which is Esther his cousin's daughter: for she had neither father nor mother. And she was a fair and fine damsel. And when her father and her mother were dead, Mordecai took her for a daughter.

And it came to pass, when the king's commandment and the king's law were heard, and many damsels were brought home to Shushan the palace, under the hand of Hegai, that Esther also was taken into the king's house, under the hand of Hegai the keeper of the damsels.

And the damsel pleased him, and she found mercy in his sight. And he hasted with her jewels, that he might give her her portion, and seven fair damsels of the king's house with her. He put her and her maids in the best place in the women's room.
And Esther told him not of her people, nor of her friendship: for Mordecai had commanded her that she should not tell.
And Mordecai walked every day before the court in the chamber of the women, to know whether it was well with Esther, and what might befall her.

And it came to pass, when the time was come for every damsel to come to king Ahasuerus, after she had been twelve months in adorning herself, (for her adorning must have been so much time, six months with balm and myrrh, and six months with good spices, that the damsels were adorned,)
Then went a damsel unto the king, and whomsoever she would, they gave her, that should go with her from the chamber of women unto the king's house.

And it came to pass, when one was come in at even, that she went out of him in the morning into the other chamber, under the hand of Saashgah the king's chamberlain, the keeper of the concubines. And she came not again to the king, except the king lusted, and called her by name.

And it came to pass, when the time was come for Esther the daughter of Abihail the cousin of Mordecai, whom he had taken for a daughter, to come to the king, that she desired nothing, save what Hegai the king's chamberlain, the keeper of the women, spake. And Esther found grace in the sight of all them that looked on her.
And Esther was taken unto king Ahasuerus into the king's house in the tenth month, which is called Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
And the king loved Esther above all women, and she found grace and mercy in his sight. above< all virgins. And he set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen in Vashti's stead.
And the king made a great feast unto all his princes and his servants. Servants (which was a feast for Esther's sake) and let the countries rest, and gave out royal gifts.
And when virgins were gathered together the second time, Mordecai sat in the king's gate.
And Esther had not yet declared her friendship, nor her people, as Mordecai had commanded her. For Esther did according to the word of Mordecai, as though he were her guardian.
At the same time that Mordecai sat in the king's gate, two of the king's chamberlains, Bigthan and Theres, which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay their hands on king Ahasuerus.
And it was known unto Mordecai, and he spake it unto Esther the queen; and Esther spake it unto the king in Mordecai's name.
And when they searched for them, they found them. And they were both hanged upon trees, and were written in the book of the chronicles before the king.
According to these acts king Ahasuerus magnified Haman the son of Medatha the Agagite, and exalted him, and set over his throne all the princes that were with him.
And all the king's servants that were in the king's gate bowed the knee, and worshipped Haman: for the king had so commanded. But Mordecai bowed not his knees, nor worshipped.
And the king's servants that were in the king's gate said unto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the king's commandment?
And when they had said these things unto him daily, and he obeyed them not, they told Haman, that they might see whether the doings of Mordecai would stand: for he had told them that he was a Jew.
And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not his knees to him, nor worshipped him, he was filled with wrath.

And he despised to lay hands on Mordecai alone, because they had told him the people of Mordecai: but he sought to destroy the people of Mordecai, all the Jews that were in all the kingdom of Ahasuerus.
In the first month, which is the moon Nisan, in the twelfth year of king Ahasuerus, was the lot cast before Haman from day to day, and from the month to the twelfth month, which is the moon Adar.

And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a people scattered, and divided among all nations, throughout all the coasts of thy kingdom; and their law is diverse from all nations, and they do not the king's statutes: and it is not meet for the king to suffer them to do so.
If it please the king, let him write that it be put to death: and I will weigh ten thousand talents of silver in the hand of the officers, and bring it into the king's chamber.
And the king took off his ring from off his hand, and gave it unto Haman the son of Medatha the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.
And the king said unto Haman, Let the silver be given thee, and the people with thee, that thou mayest do therewith as it pleaseth thee.

Then the king's scribes were called on the thirteenth day of the first month: and it was written, as Haman commanded, unto the king's princes, and to the governors to and fro in the countries, and to the captains of every people in the countries to and fro, according to the writing of every people, and according to their language, in the name of king Ahasuerus, and sealed with the king's rings.

And the letters were sent by the runners into all the king's provinces, to destroy, to slay, and to kill all the Jews, both young and old, children and women, in one day, even in the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the moon Adar, and to spoil their substance.
So the content of the scripture was, that a commandment should be given in all countries, to open unto all nations, that they should be sent unto the same day.

And the runners went out in haste, according to the king's commandment. And there was a commandment posted in Shushan the palace. And the king and Haman did eat and drink: but the city of Shushan went astray.
And when Mordecai heard all that was done, he rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the midst of the city. And he cried with a loud cry.
And he came unto the king's gate. For no man had to enter into the king's gate with sackcloth on.
And in every land, whither the king's word and commandment came, there was great mourning among the Jews; and many fasted, and wept, and mourned, and lay in sackcloth and ashes.

And Esther's damsels and her chamberlains came and told her. And the queen was sore afraid. And she sent garments, that Mordecai might put them on, and put off the sackcloth from him: but he took them not.
Then Esther called Hathach of the king's chamberlains, which stood before her, and commanded him to Mordecai, that she might know what these things were, and why he did so.
Then Hathach went out to Mordecai unto the street of the city, which was before the king's gate.
And Mordecai told him all that he had met with, and the sum of the silver that Haman had spoken, to weigh it in the king's chamber for the Jews' sakes, to destroy them.

And he gave him the copy of the commandment that was written in Shushan to destroy her, to shew it unto Esther, and to declare it unto her, and to command her to go in unto the king, and to make supplication unto him for her people.
And when Hathach was come in, and saw Esther the words of Mordecai,
And Esther spake unto Hathach, and commanded him to Mardachai:

All the king's servants, and the people of the king's provinces, know that whosoever goeth in unto the king within the court, whether he be man or woman, and is not called, he shall surely die, except the king give him the golden sceptre, that he may live. But I have not been called to go in to the king for thirty days.
And the words of Esther were spoken unto Mordecai;
And Mordecai said unto Esther again, Remember not that thou savest thy life, because thou art in the king's house, before all the Jews;

For if thou shalt keep silence at this time, then shall help and salvation come unto the Jews out of another place, and thou shalt perish, thou and thy father's house. And who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for this time?
Esther called Mordecai to answer:

Go therefore, gather together all the Jews that are in Shushan, and fast for me, that ye eat not, nor drink, day nor night, three days: so will I and my damsels fast. So I will go in to the king against the commandment, and if I perish, I perish.
And Mordecai went and did all that Esther commanded him.

And it came to pass on the third day, that Esther arrayed herself royally, and stood in the court of the king's house within the king's house. And the king sat in his royal seat in the king's house, toward the door of the house.

And when the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, she found grace in his sight. And the king stretched forth the golden scepter in his hand toward Esther. And Esther came near, and touched the point of the sceptre.
And the king said unto her, What is the matter with thee, Esther the queen? and what demandest thou? half the kingdom also shall be given thee.
And Esther said, If it please the king, let the king and Haman come this day to the feast which I have prepared.
And the king said, Make haste that Haman do what Esther hath said. And it came to pass, when the king and Haman were come to the banquet that Esther had prepared,
And the king said unto Esther, when he had drunk wine, What askest thou, Esther? It shall be given thee. And what askest thou? Even the half of the kingdom, it shall be done.
And Esther answered and said, My petition and my desire is this:

If I have found favour in the sight of the king, and if it please the king to give me my petition, and to do my desire, let the king and Haman come to the banquet which I will prepare for them; and I will do to morrow as the king hath said.
And Haman went out that day cheerful and of good cheer. And when he saw Mordecai in the king's gate, that he arose not, nor moved himself before him, he was filled with wrath against him. Mordecai.
But he abstained. And when he was come home, he sent and fetched his friends, and Seresh his wife.
And he told them the glory of his riches, and the multitude of his children, and all how the king had made him so great, and that he was exalted above the princes and servants of the king.
And Haman said, Esther the queen hath sent no man to come with the king to the feast which she hath prepared, save me: and to morrow I am summoned unto her with the king.
But in all this I have no sufficiency, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate.

And Seresh his wife and all his friends said unto him, Make a tree fifty cubits high, and tell the king to morrow to hang Mordecai thereon; and thou shalt come to supper with the king rejoicing. And it pleased Haman well, and he made a tree.
That night the king could not sleep, and commanded the chronicles and the histories to be brought. Then they were read before the king,
And it came to pass, when it was written, as Mordecai had said, that the king's two chamberlains, Bigthan and Theres, which kept the threshold, had sought to lay hands on Ahasuerus the king.
And the king said, What honour and good have we done unto Mordecai? Then said the king's boys that ministered unto him: Nothing hath happened unto him.
And the king said, Who is in the court? (For Haman was gone into the court, without the king's house, to tell the king to hang Mordecai upon the tree which he had prepared for him).
And the king's sons said unto him, Behold, Haman standeth in the court. And the king said, Let him come in.

And when Haman was come in, the king said unto him, What shall be done to the man whom the king delighteth to honour? And Haman said in his heart, To whom else would the king delight to do honour, but to me?
And Haman said unto the king: The man the king was pleased to honor,
Bring the king's royal robes, which the king is accustomed to wear, and the horse on which the king rides, and put the royal crown upon his head.

And they shall give such a garment and such a horse into the hand of one of the king's princes, that he may put on the man whom the king delighteth to honour; and they shall bring him on the horse into the streets of the city, and shall call before him, saying, Thus shall it be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour.

And the king said unto Haman, Make haste, and take the garment and the horse, as thou hast said, and do so unto Mordecai the Jew, which sitteth at the king's gate; and let nothing fail of all that thou hast spoken.
And Haman took the robe and the horse, and dressed Mordecai, and led him into the streets of the city, and cried before him, Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delighteth to honour.
And Mordecai came again to the king's gate. And Haman hasted home, bearing sorrow with his head covered.

And he told his wife Zeresh, and his friends, all that he had met with. And his wise men and Zeresh his wife said unto him, If Mordecai be of the seed of the Jews, before whom thou art lifted up to fall, thou canst not do any thing by him, but thou shalt fall before him.
And while they yet talked with him, the king's chamberlains came, and bade Haman come to the supper which Esther had prepared.
And when the king was come with Haman to the banquet which Esther the queen had prepared,
And the king said unto Esther the next day, when he had drunk wine, What askest thou, O Esther the queen, to be given thee? And what askest thou? Even half the kingdom, let it be done.
And Esther the queen answered and said, If I have found grace in thy sight, O king, and if it please the king, give me my life for my petition, and my people for my desire.

For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, and to be slain, and to be slain: and if God would that we should be sold for bondmen and bondwomen, I would hold my peace, but the enemy would not hurt the king.
And king Ahasuerus spake, and said unto Esther the queen, Who is he? Or where is he that may take this thing into his mind to do so?
And Esther said, The enemy and adversary is this wicked Haman. And Haman was astonished before the king and the queen.

And the king arose from supper and wine in his wrath, and went into the garden of the house. And Haman arose, and besought Esther the queen for his life: for he saw that the king's evil was already prepared for him.

And when the king was come again out of the garden of the house into the hall where they had eaten, Haman lay by the bench where Esther sat. And the king said, Will he strangle the queen in my house? And when the word came out of the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.

And Harbonah the chamberlain, one before the king, said, Behold, there is a tree in the house of Haman fifty cubits high, which he had made for Mordecai, which spake good for the king. And the king said, Let him hang upon it.
So they hanged Haman upon the tree which he had made Mordecai. And the king's anger was abated.
In that day king Ahasuerus gave to Esther the queen the house of Haman the enemy of the Jews. And Mordecai came before the king: for Esther told how he belonged unto her.
And the king took off his finger, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.
And Esther spake again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and besought him that he would put away the wickedness of Haman the Agagite, and his devices which he had devised against the Jews.
And the king stretched out the golden sceptre unto Esther. And Esther arose, and stood before the king.

And he said, If it please the king, and if I have found favour in his sight, and if it please the king, and if I please him, then let it be written, that the letters of the plots of Haman the son of Medatha the Agagite be revoked, which he wrote to destroy the Jews throughout all the king's provinces.
For how can I see the evil that shall befall my people? And how can I see my people perish?
And king Ahasuerus said unto Esther the queen, and to Mordecai the Jew, Behold, I have given the house of Haman unto Esther, and he is hanged upon a tree, because he laid his hand upon the Jews.

Now therefore write ye for the Jews, as ye please, in the king's name, and seal it with the king's ring. For the writing that was written in the king's name, and sealed with the king's ring, no man hath had to revoke.

And the king's scribes were called at that time in the third month, which is the moon of Sivan, on the three and twentieth day; and it was written, as Mordecai commanded, unto the Jews, and to the princes, and to the governors, and to the captains of the provinces, from India even unto the Moors, even an hundred and twenty and seven provinces, to every province according to their writings, and to every people according to their language, and to the Jews according to their writing and their language.
And it was written in the name of king Ahasuerus, and sealed with the king's rings. And he sent the letters by messengers riding upon young mouths,

Wherein the king gave the Jews, where they were in the cities, to assemble themselves together, and to stand for their lives, and to destroy, and to slay, and to destroy all the power of the people and of the land, which they feared, with their children and their wives, and to spoil their substance,
On one day in all the lands of king Ahasuerus, even on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the moon Adar.
And the content of the scripture was, that a commandment should be given in all countries, to open unto all nations, that the Jews should be sent in that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
And the messengers that rode upon the mouths went out quickly and in haste according to the king's word: and the commandment was posted in Shushan the palace.
And Mordecai went out from the king in royal apparel, yellow and white, and with a great crown of gold, clothed in a linen and purple mantle: and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.
But unto the Jews was light, and joy, and. Delight and honor come.

And in every land, and in every city, whither the king's word and commandment came, there was joy and gladness among the Jews, and gladness and good days; and many of the people of the land became Jews: for the fear of the Jews was upon them.

In the twelfth month, which is the moon Adar, in the thirteenth day, which the king's word and commandment had appointed to be done, in the very day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to overcome them, it came to pass that the Jews should overcome their enemies.

Then the Jews gathered themselves together in their cities, throughout all the provinces of king Ahasuerus, to lay hands on them that would do them evil. And no man could withstand them: for fear was come upon all nations.
And all the rulers of the provinces, and the princes, and the governors, and the king's officers, did exalt the Jews: for the fear of Mordecai was upon them.
For Mordecai was great in the king's house, and the rumour of him was heard in all the countries, how he increased and became great.
So the Jews smote upon all their enemies with the edge of the sword, and choked, and slew, and did according to their will upon them that were enemies unto them.
And in Shushan the Jews slew, and destroyed five hundred men.
And they slew Parsandatha, and Dalphon, and Aspatha,
Poratha, Adaliah, Aridatha,
parmastha, arisai, aridai, vajesatha,
The ten sons of Haman the son of Medatha, the enemy of the Jews: but they laid not their hands on his goods.
At that time came the number of them that were slain unto Shushan the castle before the king.

And the king said unto Esther the queen, The Jews have slain and killed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman: what will they do in the rest of the king's provinces? What will they do in the rest of the king's land? what will they give you? and what more will they ask you to do?
And Esther said, If it please the king, let him also the Jews of Shushan do to morrow according to this day's commandment, to hang the ten sons of Haman upon the tree.
And the king commanded thus. And the commandment was posted in Shushan, and the ten sons of Haman were hanged.
And the Jews gathered themselves together to Shushan on the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and slew in Shushan three hundred men: but they laid not their hands on their goods.

And the rest of the Jews that were in the king's provinces came together, and tarried for their lives, to give them rest from their enemies, and slew their enemies seventy and five thousand: but they laid not their hands on their goods.
And it came to pass on the thirteenth day of the month Adar, and they rested on the fourteenth day of that month, which was made a day of rest and gladness.
But the Jews that were at Shushan were gathered together, both on the thirteenth day and on the fourteenth day, and rested on the fifteenth day: and they made that day a day of rest and gladness.
Therefore the Jews that dwelt in the villages and in the towns made the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of feasting and gladness, and sent gifts one to another.
And Mordecai described this history, and sent letters unto all the Jews that were in all the countries of king Ahasuerus, both near and far,
And they took and kept the fourteenth and fifteenth day of the month Adar yearly,

After the days wherein the Jews were at rest from their enemies, and after the months wherein their sorrows were turned into joy, and their mourning into good days, that they should keep them for days of good living and gladness, and send gifts one to another, and communicate them to the poor.
And the Jews received it, which they began to do, and which Mordecai wrote unto them:
As Haman the son of Medatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, thought to destroy all the Jews, and cast lots to terrify and kill them;
And how Esther went to the king, and spake that by letters his wicked devices, which he thought against the Jews, should be turned upon his head; and how they hanged him and his sons upon the tree.
Wherefore they called these days Purim by the name of the lot, according to all the words of this epistle, and what they themselves had seen, and what had come unto them.

And the Jews set it up, and took it upon themselves, and upon their seed, and upon all that joined themselves unto them, that they would not pass over to keep these two days yearly, as they were described and appointed,

That these days should not be forgotten, but kept among their children, among all generations, in all countries, and in all cities. These are the days of Purim, which shall not be forgotten among the Jews, neither shall their remembrance perish among their seed.
And Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with all their might to confirm this other letter of Purim.
And sent letters unto all the Jews in the hundred and twenty and seven countries of the kingdom of Ahasuerus with kind and faithful words:

And they confirmed these days of Purim in their appointed time, as Mordecai the Jew had confirmed them, and Esther the queen; as they had confirmed upon their souls, and upon their seed, the story of their fasting and their crying.
And Esther commanded to confirm the history of these Purim, and to write it in a book.
And king Ahasuerus laid interest upon the land, and upon the isles of the sea.
But all the works of his power and might, and the great glory of Mordecai, which the king gave him, behold, it is written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia.

For Mordecai the Jew was the other after king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and pleasant among the multitude of his brethren, seeking good for his people, and speaking the best for all his seed.
There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. He was righteous and wicked, fearing God and shunning evil.
And begat seven sons and three daughters.

And of his cattle were seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a great many servants: and he was more glorious than all they that dwelt eastward.
And his sons went and made merry every man in his house in his day, and sent and invited their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

And it came to pass, when the day was expired, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, "My sons have sinned and blessed God in their hearts. So Job did all the days.
And it came to pass in a day, when the children of God came and stood before the LORD, that Satan also came among them.
And the LORD said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? And Satan answered the LORD, and said: I have compassed the country round about.
And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou not taken heed unto my servant Job? for there is none like him in the land, wicked and righteous, fearing God, and avoiding evil.
And Satan answered the LORD, and said, Thinkest thou that Job feareth God for nought?
Hast thou preserved him, and his house, and all that he hath round about? Thou hast blessed the work of his hands; And his substance is spread abroad in the land.
But put forth thine hand, and touch all that he hath: what matter, he will bless thee to thy face?
And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thine hand; without him alone lay not thine hand. Then Satan departed from the LORD.
And it came to pass on the day that his sons and his daughters did eat and drink wine in their brother's house, the firstborn,
And there came a messenger to Job, saying, The oxen plowed, and the asses walked beside them in the pasture;
And they of Arabia came in, and took them, and smote the lads with the edge of the sword: and I alone escaped to tell thee.
While he yet spake, another came and said, The fire of God came down from heaven, and burned up sheep and lambs, and consumed them: and I alone escaped to tell thee.
While he yet spake, there came one, and said, The Chaldeans made three points, and attacked the camels, and took them, and smote the lads with the edge of the sword: and I alone escaped to tell thee.
While he yet spake, one came and said, Thy sons and thy daughters did eat and drink in the house of their brother the firstborn;
And, behold, a great wind came from the wilderness, and brake upon the four corners of the house, and cast it upon the young men, and they died: and I alone escaped to tell thee.
And Job arose, and rent his clothes, and ruffled his head, and fell to the ground, and worshipped.
And said: I came naked from my mother's womb; naked shall I return. The LORD gave, the LORD hath taken away: blessed be the name of the LORD.
In all this Job sinned not, neither did he do anything foolish against God.
And it came to pass in the day that the children of God came and stood before the LORD, that Satan also came among them, and stood before the LORD.
Then said the LORD unto Satan, Whence comest thou? And Satan answered the LORD, and said: I have compassed the country round about.

And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou not taken heed unto my servant Job? For there is none like him in the land, wicked and righteous, fearing God, avoiding evil, and holding fast his godliness: but thou hast moved me to destroy him without a cause.
Satan answered the LORD, and said, Skin for skin; and all that a man hath he leaveth for his life.
But put forth thine hand, and touch his bones and his flesh: what matter, he will bless thee to thy face?
And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thine hand: but spare his life.
Then Satan went out from the presence of the LORD, and smote Job with evil swarms from the sole of his foot even to the top of his head.
And he took a potsherd, and scraped himself, and sat in the ashes.
And his wife said unto him, Dost thou yet hold fast thy devotion? Yes, bless God and die!
And he said unto her, Thou speakest as foolish women speak. Have we received good from God, and should we not also receive evil? In all this Job sinned not with his lips.

And when the three friends of Job heard all the evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place, Eliphaz of Theman, and Bildad of Shuah, and Zophar of Naamah. They were united in coming to lament and comfort him.
And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, they knew him not, and lifted up their voice, and wept; and every man rent his clothes, and sprinkled earth upon their heads toward heaven.
And they sat with him upon the earth seven days and seven nights, and spake nothing to him: for they saw that the sorrow was very great.
After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed his day.
And Job said:
Let the day be lost wherein I was born, and the night when it was said, A man is conceived.
that same day must be dark, and GOD from above must not inquire of it; no brightness must shine upon it.
Darkness and gloom shall overtake him, and thick clouds shall be upon him, and the vapour by day shall make him hideous.
Let the night take a darkness, and not rejoice among the days of the year, nor come into the number of the moons.
Behold, the night shall be lonely, and there shall be no rejoicing therein.
They curse the cursers of the day, and they that are ready to raise up Leviathan.
Her stars must be dark in her twilight; she hopeth for the light, and cometh not, nor seeth the eyebrows of the dawn,
That she hath not shut the door of my womb, nor hid evil from mine eyes.
Why did I not die from my mother's womb? Why did I not perish when I came out of the womb?
Why have they set me in the lap? Why am I suckled with breasts?
I would lie down and be still, and sleep, and be at rest.
With the kings and counsellors of the earth, which build the wilderness;
Or with the princes that have gold, and their houses are full of silver;
or like an untimely birth hidden and nothing would be, like the young children who have never seen the light.
There shall the wicked cease from their raging: there shall they rest that have laboured much.
For the captives are at peace with one another, and hear not the voice of the oppressor.
There are both small and great, servant and he that is set free of his master.
Why is light given to the weary, and life to the afflicted heart?
Who wait for death, and come not, and dig it out of secret,
Who almost rejoice, and are glad to get the grave:)
And to the man whose way is hid, and God covereth it from him?
For when I shall eat, I groan, and my weeping cometh forth like water.
For that which I feared is come upon me, and that which I cared for is come upon me.
Was I not blissful? Was I not fine quiet? Was I not well at rest? And comes such unrest!
Then Eliphaz of Theman answered and said:
Thou mayest not like it, if any man try to speak unto thee: but who can refrain?
Behold, thou hast instructed many, and hast strengthened hands;
Thy speech hath lifted up the fallen, and thou hast strengthened the trembling knees.
But when it cometh upon thee, thou shalt be weak: and when it cometh upon thee, thou shalt be afraid.
is this your (God's) fear, comfort, hope, and godliness?
Thinkest thou, where hath the innocent perished, or where hath the righteous ever been destroyed?
As I have seen them plow toil, and sow mischief, and they also reap it,
That they should perish by the breath of God, and be consumed by the spirit of his wrath.
The roaring of the lions, and the voice of the great lions, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
The lion is consumed, that he rob no more: and the young of the lioness are scattered.
And there came unto me a secret word, and mine ear received a word of it.
When I have beheld visions in the night, when sleep falleth upon men,
Then fear and trembling came upon me, and all my bones were troubled.
And when the Spirit passed over before me, the hair of my head stood on end in my flesh.
And there stood a vision before mine eyes, and I knew not the form thereof: it was still, and I heard a voice:
How can a man be more righteous than God, or a man more pure than he who made him?
Behold, there is none without blame among his servants, and he findeth folly in his messengers.
How many more of them that dwell in the houses of clay, and that are founded upon the earth, shall be eaten of the worms?
From the morning until the evening they are cut off, and before they know it they are gone;
And the remnant of them perish, and die also unawares.
Name me one; what matter if thou find one? And look around thee for any saint.
But wrath slayeth a foolish man, and zeal slayeth a foolish man.
I saw a fool rooted up, and I suddenly cursed his house.
His children shall be far from salvation, and shall be broken in the gate, because there shall be no saviour.
His harvest shall the hungry eat, and the armed shall take him, and his goods shall the thirsty drink.
For trouble cometh not out of the earth, neither doth mischief grow out of the field,
but man is born to misfortune, as the birds hover to soar.
But I will now speak of God and act from Him,
Who doeth great things that cannot be searched out, and wonders that cannot be numbered;
Who giveth rain upon the land, and causeth water to come upon the streets.
He that exalteth the lowly, and lifteth up the afflicted.
He bringeth to nought the devices of the crafty, that their hand may not execute them.
He fähet the wise in their craftiness, and overthroweth the counsel of the perverse,
That they may walk in darkness by day, and grope in the south as in the night;
And delivereth the poor from the sword, and from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty;
And the hope of the poor is, that wickedness shall shut her mouth.
Behold, blessed is the man whom God punisheth: therefore refuse not the chastening of the Almighty.
For he woundeth and bindeth up; he breaketh in pieces, and his hand healeth.
Out of six tribulations shall he deliver thee; and in the seventh no evil shall touch thee.
He shall deliver thee from death in tribulation, and from the hand of the sword in war.
He shall hide thee from the scourge of the tongue, that thou fear not destruction when it cometh.
In destruction and hunger thou shalt laugh, and shalt not be afraid of the wild beasts of the land,
But thy covenant shall be with the stones of the field, and the wild beasts of the earth shall keep peace with thee;
And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle is at peace; and thou shalt keep thy dwelling, and shalt not sin;
And thou shalt know that thy seed shall be multiplied, and thy seed as the grass of the earth;
And thou shalt come to the grave in old age, as sheaves are brought in in their season.
Behold, we have searched it out, and it is so; obey it, and mark it.
Job answered and said:
If my sorrow were weighed, and my affliction put into a balance together,
It would be heavier than the sand of the sea: therefore all that I say is vain.
For the arrows of the Almighty are in me, the fury of the Almighty drinketh out of my spirit, and the terrors of God are upon me.
The deer crieth not when he hath grass; the ox bleateth not when he hath his meat.
can you also eat that is unsalted? Or who likes to taste the white around the yolk?
That which my soul hateth to touch is the meat of my sorrows.
O that my request might be granted, and that God might give me that which I hope for!
That God would begin, and smite me, and let his hand go, and break me in pieces!
Then would I have consoled myself, and prayed in my sickness that he would not spare me. I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
What is my strength, that I may persevere? and what is my end, that my soul should be patient?
If my strength be not of stone, my flesh is not of brass.
for I have nowhere to turn, and my fortune is gone.
He that refuseth mercy to his neighbour putteth away the fear of the Almighty.
My brethren pass away contemptuously before me, as a brook, as the rivers of waters pass by.
But they that are afraid of the frost, upon them shall the snow fall.
In time, when the heat shall oppress them, they shall faint; and when it is hot, they shall perish from their place.
Their way goeth out by the way side; they tread upon the rough places, and perish.
They look to the ways of Thema; to the paths of Reicharabia they wait.
But they shall be ashamed when it is most sure, and shall be ashamed when they come to it.
For ye are now come unto me: and seeing sorrow, ye fear.
Did I also say, Bring ye hither, and of your substance give me?
And delivereth me out of the hand of the enemy, and delivereth me out of the hand of tyrants?
Teach me, and I will hold my peace: and that which I know not, instruct me.
Why do ye reprove right speech? Who is there among you who can punish them?
Ye devise words to punish, and ye pause words to make me despondent.
Ye fall upon a poor orphan, and dig pits for your neighbour.
But because ye have lifted up, look upon me, whether I will stand before you in lies.
Answer what is right; my answer will still remain right.
What matter if my tongue be false, and my mouth speak evil?
Must not man always be at strife upon the earth, and his days be as the days of a hired servant?
As a servant longs for a shadow, and a hired servant for his work to be done,
So I have labored in vain for whole moons, and miserable nights have been many to me.
And when I lay down, I said, When shall I rise? And after that I reckoned when it was evening: for I was altogether an abomination to every man, until it was dark.
My flesh is worm-eaten and boil-eaten round about: my skin is shrivelled up, and is become ruinous.
My days have flown away lighter than a weaver's bobbin, and have passed away, that there hath been no stopping.
Remember that my life is a wind, and mine eyes come not again to see the good.
and no living eye shall see me any more. Thine eyes look upon me; At this I perish.
A cloud passeth away, and fadeth away: so he that goeth down to hell cometh not up again.
And he cometh not again into his house, and his place knoweth him no more.
Therefore also I will not withhold my mouth; I will speak of the anguish of my heart, and I will testify of the affliction of my soul.
Am I then a sea, or a whale, that thou hast kept me thus?
When I have thought, my bed shall comfort me, my couch shall make me light;
when I speak to myself, thou terrifieth me with dreams, and makest me afraid,
My soul desireth to be hanged, and my bones to die.
I desire no more to live. Cease from me, for my days have been in vain.
What is a man, that thou esteemest him great, and art troubled with him?
Thou visitest him daily, and tryest him every hour.
Why dost thou not depart from me, and dost not cease from me, till I have swallowed up my spittle?
If I have sinned, what shall I do unto thee, O thou keeper of men? Why makest thou me to stumble upon thee, and art a burden unto myself?
And why forgivest thou not my iniquity, and takest not away my sin? For now will I lie down in the earth; and when they seek me to morrow, I shall not be there.
Then answered Bildad of Suah, and said:
How long wilt thou speak these things, and let the speech of thy mouth be so proud?
Thinkest thou that God doth judge unjustly, or that the Almighty doth pervert justice?
If thy sons have sinned before him, he hath cast them off for their iniquity.
But if thou turn in time unto God, and beseech the Almighty,
And if thou be pure and upright, he will awake unto thee, and will set up the tabernacle again for thy righteousness' sake;
And what at first thou hadst little, hereafter thou shalt almost increase.
For inquire of the former generations, and take upon thee to inquire of their fathers.
(For we are of old, and know nothing; our life is a shadow upon the earth.)
They shall teach thee, and tell thee, and bring forth their speech out of their heart.
Can the reed grow up where it is not wet, or grass grow without water?
Or else, if it be yet in the flower, before it be cut down, it withereth before they make hay.
So it is with all those who forget God, and the hope of the hypocrites will be lost.
For his confidence is gone, and his hope is a cobweb.
He shall rely upon his house, and yet shall not stand: he shall keep it, and yet shall not stand.
It is fruitful before the sun: and the branches of his garden grow up.
His seed is thick by the springs, and his house is built upon the stones.
But if he swallow him up out of his place, he shall stand against him, as if he knew him not.
Behold, this is the joy of his being; and others shall grow out of the dust.
Therefore, behold, God does not reject the righteous, nor does He uphold the hand of the wicked,
Until thy mouth be full of laughter, and thy lips of rejoicing.
But they that hate thee shall be put to shame, and the tabernacle of the wicked shall not stand.
Job answered and said:
Yea, I know almost well that therefore a man may not stand justified against God.
If he desire to dispute with him, he cannot answer him one to a thousand.
He is wise and mighty: who hath ever succeeded that hath set himself against him?
He removeth mountains before they know it, whom he turneth back in his wrath.
He causeth a land to depart out of her place, and her pillars to shake.
He saith unto the sun, let it not rise, and seal up the stars.
He spreadeth out the heavens alone, and walketh upon the waves of the sea.
He maketh the chariot in the heavens, and Orion, and the mother hen, and the stars toward the south.
He doeth great things which cannot be searched out, and wonders of which there is no number.
Behold, he passeth over before me before I know it, and is changed before I know it.
Behold, if he go quickly, who shall repeat him? Who shall say unto him, What doest thou?
He is GOD, his wrath no man can quench; under him the proud lords must bow down.
How then shall I answer him, and find words against him?
Though I be right, yet cannot I answer him, but I must plead my right.
Though I call upon him, and he heareth me, yet will I not believe that he heareth my voice.
For he hath overtaken me with violence, and hath given me many wounds without cause.
He restoreth not my spirit, but maketh me full of sorrow.
If I desire power, he is too mighty: if I desire judgment, who will be my witness?
If I say that I am righteous, he condemneth me: if I am righteous, he maketh me unrighteous.
If then I be godly, my soul shall not take it. I desire no more life.
