Saying, The LORD seeth it not, and the God of Jacob regardeth it not.
Mark you, ye fools of the people, and ye fools, when will ye be wise?
He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? He that made the eye, shall he not see?
He that chasteneth the heathen, shall he not chasten? he that teacheth men what they know.
But the LORD knoweth the thoughts of men, that they are vain.
Blessed is he whom thou, O LORD, chastenest, and teachest by thy law,
That he may have patience in the day of evil, until the pit be prepared for the wicked.
For the LORD will not cast off his people, nor forsake his inheritance.
For the law must be the law, and all godly hearts will fall unto it.
Who shall stand with me against the wicked? Who shall stand with me against the workers of iniquity?
If the LORD help me not, my soul shall lie in silence.
And I said, My foot stumbled; but thy mercy, O LORD, kept me.
I had many sorrows in my heart: but thy consolations made my soul glad.
Thou shalt never be one with the pernicious chair, which interpreteth the law falsely.
They prepare themselves against the soul of the righteous, and condemn innocent blood.
But the LORD is my refuge; my God is the stronghold of my confidence.
And he shall recompense their iniquity, and shall destroy them for their wickedness: the LORD our God shall destroy them.
Come ye near, and let us rejoice in the LORD, and shout for joy to the stronghold of our salvation.
Let us come before his face with thanksgiving, and with psalms let us shout for him.
For the LORD is a great God, and a great King above all gods.
For in his hand is that which the earth bringeth forth; and the high places of the mountains are his also.
For his is the sea, and he hath made it; and his hands have prepared the dry land.
Come, let us worship, and kneel, and fall down before the LORD that made us.
For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. This day, if ye hear his voice,
Then harden not your heart, as it was in Meribah, as it was in Massa in the wilderness,
When your fathers tempted me, they felt and saw my work,
That I had forty years' trouble with this people, saying, They are men whose hearts always desire the wrong way, and will not learn my ways;
That I sware in mine anger, They shall not come into my rest.
Sing to the Lord a new song; sing to the Lord, all the earth!
Sing unto the LORD, and praise his name; preach one day upon another his salvation.
Declare his glory among the heathen, his wonders among all nations.
For the LORD is great and greatly to be praised, marvellous above all gods.
For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the LORD hath made heaven.
It is glorious and marvellous before him; it is mighty and glorious in his sanctuary.
O ye nations, bring unto the LORD, bring unto the LORD glory and power.
Bring ye hither unto the LORD the glory of his name; bring ye gifts, and come into his courts.
To the LORD in holy ornaments; let all the earth fear him.
Say among the heathen that the LORD is king, and hath prepared his kingdom, as far as the earth is, to abide in it, and judgeth the nations aright.
Be glad, and let the earth rejoice; let the sea roar, and all that is therein;
Let the field be glad, and all that is therein: and let all the trees of the forest praise.
Before the LORD: for he cometh, because he cometh to judge the earth. He shall judge the earth with righteousness, and the nations with his truth.
The LORD is king: let the earth rejoice, and let the isles be glad, as many as are therein.
Clouds and darkness are round about him. Righteousness and judgment is the stronghold of his throne:
Fire goeth before him, and kindleth his enemies round about.
His lightnings shall shine upon the ground: the earth shall see, and be afraid.
Mountains melt like wax before the LORD, before the ruler of all the earth.
the heavens declare his righteousness, and all nations behold his glory.
Let all them be ashamed that serve images, and that boast of idols. Worship him, all gods!
Zion heareth, and is glad; and the daughters of Judah rejoice, O LORD, in thy government.
For thou, O LORD, art the most high in all the earth: thou art greatly exalted above all gods.
Ye that love the LORD, hate evil. The LORD preserveth the souls of his saints: from the hand of the wicked shall he deliver them.
The light must always dawn upon the righteous, and joy upon the devout heart.
Ye righteous, rejoice in the LORD; and give thanks unto him, and glorify his holiness.
A psalm. Sing unto the LORD a new song: for he doeth wonders. He triumpheth with his right hand, and with his holy arm.
The LORD hath declared his salvation, and hath shewed his righteousness before the nations.
He remembereth his mercy and truth unto the house of Israel. The ends of the earth behold the salvation of our God.
Rejoice unto the LORD, all the earth: sing, praise, and extol.
Praise the LORD with harps, with harps, and with psalms;
With trumpets and trumpets shout for joy before the Lord the King.
The sea roareth, and that which is therein, the ground, and they that dwell therein.
Let the rivers rejoice, and let all the mountains be glad.
Before the LORD: for he cometh to judge the earth. He shall judge the earth with righteousness, and the nations with judgment.
The LORD is king, therefore the nations rage: he sitteth upon cherubims, therefore the world stirs.
The LORD is great in Zion, and high above all nations.
thanks be unto thy great and marvellous name, which is holy.
In the kingdom of this king is justice loved. Thou givest godliness; thou establishest judgment and righteousness in Jacob.
Exalt the LORD our God, worship at his footstool: for he is holy.
Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among them that call upon his name: they cried unto the LORD, and he hearkened unto them.
He spake unto them by a pillar of cloud. They kept his testimonies and commandments which he gave them.
O LORD, thou art our God, thou hast heard them; thou, O God, hast forgiven them, and hast punished their doings:
Exalt the LORD our God, and worship in his holy mountain: for the LORD our God is holy:
a psalm of thanksgiving. Rejoice in the Lord, all the earth!
Serve the LORD with gladness; come before his face with joy.
Know ye that the LORD is GOD: he hath made us, and not we ourselves, his people, and sheep of his pasture.
Enter ye into his gates with thanksgiving, into his courts with praise: give thanks unto him, praise his name.
For the LORD is good, and his mercy endureth for ever, and his truth for ever.
A psalm of David. Of grace and judgment will I sing, and praise thee, O LORD.
I will deal carefully and truly with them that are mine, and walk faithfully in my house.
I take no evil thing for myself. I hate the transgressor and will not let him stay with me.
A wicked heart must depart from me: I will not suffer the wicked.
He that slandereth his neighbour in secret, him will I destroy. I do not like him who is proud and bold.
Mine eyes are upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me: and I delight to have godly servants.
I will not keep men in my house: liars do not prosper with me.
Early will I destroy all the wicked of the land, and cut off all the transgressors from the city of the LORD.
A prayer of the wretched, when he is distressed, and poureth out his complaint before the Lord.
O Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come unto thee.
Hide not thy face from me in trouble: incline thine ear unto me: when I call upon thee, hear me quickly.
For my days are passed away like smoke, and my bones are burned up like a fire.
My heart is smitten, and withered like grass, that I also forget to eat my bread.
my bones cling to my flesh with weeping and groaning.
I am like a bittern in the wilderness; I am like an owl in the disturbed places.
I wake up and I am like a lonely bird on the roof.
Mine enemies reproach me daily; and they that mock me swear by me.
For I eat ashes as bread, and mix my drink with wines.
From thy wrath and from thy anger, because thou hast lifted me up, and cast me down to the ground.
My days are gone as a shadow; and I wither as grass.
But thou, O LORD, shalt endure for ever, and thy memorial for ever.
Arise, and have mercy on Zion: for the time is come for thee to have mercy upon her, and the hour is come.
For thy servants would gladly build her, and would gladly see her stones and her lime dressed;
That the heathen may fear the name of the LORD, and all the kings of the earth thy glory;
That the LORD should build Zion, and appear in his glory.
He turneth to the prayer of the forsaken, and spurneth not their prayer.
Let this be written in the generations to come: and the people that shall be created shall praise the LORD.
For he looketh from his holy height, and the LORD looketh from heaven to earth,
That he may hear the groaning of the prisoner, and loose the children of death,
That they might preach the name of the LORD in Zion, and his praise in Jerusalem,
When the nations shall come together, and the kingdoms to serve the LORD.
He hath humbled my strength in the way; he hath shortened my days.
I say: My God, do not take me away in the half of my days! Your years shall last for and for.
Thou hast founded the earth before, and the heavens are the work of thy hands.
They will pass away, but you will remain. They shall all perish like a garment; they shall be changed like a garment, when thou shalt change them.
But thou remainest as thou art, and thy years have no end.
The children of thy servants shall abide, and their seed shall flourish before thee.
a psalm of David. Praise the LORD, O my soul, and that which is within me, his holy name.
Praise the LORD, O my soul, and forget not the good things which he hath done thee,
Who forgiveth all thy sins, and healeth all thine infirmities,
Who redeemeth thy life from destruction, who crowneth thee with grace and mercy,
Who maketh thy mouth to rejoice, and thou shalt be young again as the eagle.
The LORD executeth righteousness and judgment unto all that are wronged.
He hath made known his ways unto Moses, and his doings unto the children of Israel.
Merciful and gracious is the LORD, patient, and of great kindness.
He shall not always be angry, nor hold wrath for ever.
He dealeth not with us according to our sins, neither recompenseth us according to our iniquities.
For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so he hath mercy on them that fear him.
As far as the morning is from the evening, let our transgression be from us.
As a father hath mercy on his children, so hath the LORD mercy on them that fear him.
For he knoweth what manner of things we are: he remembereth that we are dust.
A man in his life is as grass; he flourisheth as a flower of the field.
When the wind passeth over it, it is no more, neither knoweth it any more the place thereof.
But the mercy of the LORD endureth for ever upon them that fear him, and his righteousness upon the children of children.
In them that keep his covenant, and remember his commandments, to do them.
The LORD hath prepared his throne in heaven, and his kingdom ruleth over all.
Praise ye the LORD, O ye his angels, ye mighty men of valour, which do his commandment, that the voice of his word may be heard.
Praise ye the LORD, all ye his hosts, his servants, which do his will.
Praise the LORD, all his works, in all places of his dominion! Praise the LORD, my soul!
Praise the LORD, O my soul. O LORD my God, thou art very glorious; thou art beautifully and splendidly adorned.
Light is thy garment which thou hast put on. You spread out the sky like a carpet;
thou archest it above with water; thou goest upon the clouds as upon a chariot, and walkest upon the wings of the wind.
Who makest thine angels winds, and thy servants flames of fire;
Thou that layest the foundation of the earth upon his ground, that it may abide for ever and ever.
With the deep thou coverest it as with a garment, and waters stand upon the mountains.
But from thy rebuke they flee, from thy thunder they go away.
The mountains go up, and the broad places come down to the place which thou hast founded for them.
you have set a boundary, they do not come over it, and do not have to cover the ground again.
Thou hast caused wells to spring up in the valleys, and the waters to flow between the mountains,
That all the beasts of the field may drink, and that the beasts of the field may quench their thirst.
In the same sit the birds of the air, and sing under the branches.
Thou dost wet the mountains from above; thou makest the land full of fruit which thou makest.
Thou hast caused grass to grow for cattle, and seed for the use of men, to bring forth bread out of the ground,
And that the wine may gladden the heart of man, and that his form may be made beautiful with oil, and that the bread may strengthen the heart of man;
The trees of the LORD are full of sap, the cedars of Lebanon, which he hath planted.
There the birds make their nests, and the herons dwell in the fir trees.
the high mountains are the refuge of the chamois, and the clefts of the rabbits.
Thou makest the moon to divide the year after; the sun knoweth her going down.
Thou makest darkness, and night cometh; and all the wild beasts stir up,
The young lions that roar after the prey, and seek their meat from GOD.
But when the sun riseth, they lift themselves up, and lie down in their holes.
So man goeth forth to his work, and to his labour, until the even.
O LORD, how great and abundant are thy works! Thou hast wisely arranged them all, and the earth is full of thy goods.
The sea, which is so great and wide, teemeth without number, both beasts great and small.
There go the ships: there are whales which thou hast made to jest within.
All things wait for thee, that thou mayest give them meat in his season.
When thou givest unto them, they gather: when thou openest thine hand, they are filled with good.
When thou hidest thy face, they are afraid; when thou takest away their breath, they perish, and return to dust.
Thou sendest forth thy breath, and they are made; and thou renewest the form of the earth.
The glory of the LORD is everlasting: the LORD is well pleased with his works.
He looketh upon the earth, and it quaketh: he toucheth the mountains, and they smoke.
I will sing unto the LORD all the days of my life, and praise my God as long as I live.
Let my speech please him. I rejoice in the LORD.
Let there be an end of sinners on earth, and let the wicked be no more! Praise the Lord, my soul! Hallelujah!
Give thanks unto the LORD, and preach his name; declare his doings among the nations;
Sing of him, and praise him; speak of all his wonders;
Praise his holy name; let the heart of them that seek the LORD rejoice.
Inquire ye of the LORD, and of his power; seek his face always.
Remember his wondrous works which he hath done, his miracles, and his word,
You, the seed of Abraham his servant, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones!
He is the LORD our God: he judgeth in all the earth.
He remembereth his covenant for ever, the word which he promised for many thousands to come and to go.
Which he made with Abraham, and of the oath with Isaac,
And established the same Jacob for a law, and Israel for an everlasting covenant.
And said, Unto thee will I give the land of Canaan, the lot of your inheritance,
For they were few and poor, and strangers within.
And they went from nation to nation, from kingdom to kingdom.
He suffered no man to harm them, and punished kings for their sakes.
do not touch my anointed, and do not harm my prophets.
And he caused a famine to come into the land, and took away all the supply of bread.
And he sent a man before them; and Joseph was sold for a servant.
They constrained his feet in the stocks, and his body was made to lie in irons,
Till his word came, and the speech of the LORD purified him.
And the king sent, and loosed him: and the lord of nations loosed him.
And he made him lord of his house, and ruler over all his goods,
That he might instruct his princes after his manner, and teach his ancients wisdom.
And Israel went into Egypt, and Jacob was a stranger in the land of Ham.
And he increased his people greatly, and made them mightier than their enemies.
He turned away their hearts, so that they were angry with his people, and thought to subdue his servants with guile.
And he sent his servant Moses, Aaron, whom he had chosen.
These did his signs among them, and his wonders in the land of Ham.
He caused darkness to come, and made it dark; and were not disobedient to his words.
He turned their waters into blood, and killed their fish.
Their land swarmed with toads out of the chambers of their kings.
He said, There came vermin, lice, in all their borders.
He gave them hail for rain, flames of fire in their land;
And he smote their vines and their fig trees, and brake the trees within their borders.
And he said, There came locusts and beetles without number.
And they did eat all the grass of their land, and did eat the fruit of their field.
And smote all the firstborn in Egypt, all their firstborn heirs.
And he brought them out with silver and gold; and there was not an infirm man among their tribes.
And Egypt was glad that they went out: for their fear was fallen upon them.
And he spread out a cloud for a covering, and a fire to shine by night.
And they asked, and he sent for quails; and he filled them with bread from heaven.
And he opened the rock, and waters flowed out, and streams ran in the dry wilderness.
For he remembered his holy word, spoken unto Abraham his servant.
So he brought forth his people with joy, and his elect with gladness.
And gave them the lands of the heathen, that they might take the goods of the nations.
That they might keep his statutes, and keep his judgments. Hallelujah!
Hallelujah! Give thanks unto the LORD: for he is good; and his mercy endureth for ever.
Who can utter the great deeds of the LORD, and praise all his praiseworthy works?
Blessed are they that keep the commandment, and do right continually.
Remember me, O LORD, according to the mercy which thou hast promised thy people: show us thy help,
That we may see the welfare of thine elect, and rejoice that it is well with thy people, and glory in thine inheritance.
We have sinned with our fathers; we have transgressed, we have been ungodly.
Our fathers in Egypt would not understand thy wonders; they remembered not thy great goodness, and were disobedient at the sea, even at the Red sea.
And he helped them for his name's sake, to shew forth his power.
And he rebuked the Red sea, and it was dry: and he led them through the deep as through a wilderness;
And delivered them out of the hand of him that hated them, and delivered them out of the hand of the enemy.
And the waters drowned their adversaries, that there remained not one.
And they believed his words, and sang his praises.
But they soon forgot his works; they waited not for his counsel.
And they lusted in the wilderness, and tempted GOD in the desert.
And he gave them their request, and sent them enough until they were disgusted with it.
And they rebelled against Moses in the camp, and against Aaron the holy one of the LORD.
And the earth arose, and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram.
And fire was kindled among their company; and the flame burned up the wicked.
And they made a calf in Horeb, and worshipped the graven image;
And changed their glory into the likeness of an ox eating grass.
They forgot God their Saviour, who had done so great things in Egypt,
wonders in the land of Ham, and terrible works at the Red sea.
And he said, He would destroy them, except Moses his elect had stayed the breach, to turn away his fury, that he might not destroy them.
And they despised the dear land; they believed not his word.
And murmured in their tents; they hearkened not unto the voice of the LORD.
And he lifted up his hand against them, to smite them in the wilderness.
And cast their seed among the heathen, and scattered them abroad.
And they clave unto Baal the blood of their sons, and the blood of their daughters, which they sacrificed unto the idols of Canaan; and the land was stained with blood;
And they provoked him to anger with their doings; and the plague was upon them.
And he came to Phinehas, and settled the matter, and the plague was stayed,
And it was counted unto him for righteousness for ever and ever.
And they provoked him to anger at the water of Hader; and they afflicted Moses.
For they grieved his heart, so that some words escaped from him.
Neither did they destroy the nations, as the LORD had commanded them,
But they mingled with the heathen, and learned the works thereof,
And served their idols, which were an offence unto them.
And they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils.
And they shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and of their daughters, which they sacrificed unto the idols of Canaan, so that the land was stained with blood;
And defiled themselves with their works, and fornicated with their doings.
And the anger of the LORD was kindled against his people, and abhorred his inheritance.
And delivered them into the hand of the heathen, that they might have dominion over them which were evil to them.
And their enemies affrighted them, and were humbled under their hands.
He saved them many times: but they provoked him to anger with their pride, and became few because of their iniquity.
And he looked upon their affliction, when he heard their lamentation,
And remembered his covenant made with them. And repented him according to his great goodness.
And made them come to mercy before all them that had taken them captives.
Help us, O LORD our God, and bring us together from among the nations, that we may give thanks to thy holy name, and praise thy praise.
Blessed be the LORD God of Israel for ever and ever: and let all the people say, Amen, alleluia.
Give thanks unto the LORD: for he is good; and his mercy endureth for ever.
Say ye, ye that are redeemed by the LORD, whom he hath redeemed out of trouble.
And whom he hath gathered together out of the countries of the rising, and of the going down, and of the north, and of the sea;
Who wandered in the wilderness by the way of no man, and found no city to dwell in,
hungry and thirsty, and their soul languisheth;
And they cried unto the LORD in their affliction, and he delivered them out of their fears.
And led them in a right way, that they might go to the city where they dwelt:
They shall give thanks unto the LORD for his lovingkindness, and for his wondrous works which he doeth for the children of men,
To satisfy the thirsty soul, and to fill the hungry soul with good things.
Who were made to sit in darkness and in vanity, bound in constraint and in iron,
Because they had disobeyed the commandments of God, and had profaned the law of the Most High;
Therefore their heart was troubled with misery, because they lay there, and no man helped them;
And they cried unto the LORD in their affliction, and he saved them out of their fears.
And brought them out of darkness and gloom, and brake their bands:
They shall give thanks unto the LORD for his lovingkindness, and for his wondrous works which he doeth for the children of men,
To break the doors of brass, and to break the bars of iron.
The fools that were afflicted for their transgression, and for their sin,
And they were disgusted with all meat, and were sick unto death;
And they cried unto the LORD in their affliction, and he saved them out of their fears;
And he sent his word, and healed them, and saved them, that they died not:
They shall give thanks unto the LORD for his lovingkindness, and for his wondrous works which he doeth for the children of men,
and offer thanksgiving, and tell his works with gladness.
They that sailed in ships upon the sea, and did their trade in great waters;
Who have known the works of the LORD, and his wonders in the sea,
When he spake, and stirred up a tempest that lifted up the waves,
And they went up to heaven, and entered into the bottomless pit, and their souls were troubled for fear,
And they staggered and staggered like a drunken man, and knew not what to do;
And they cried unto the LORD in their affliction, and he brought them out of their fears.
And quieted the tempest, that the waves were subdued,
And they were glad when it was made quiet, and he brought them to land according to their desire:
They shall give thanks unto the LORD for his goodness, and for his wondrous works which he doeth for the children of men,
And glorify him among the congregation, and praise him among the ancients.
Those whose brooks were dried up, and whose fountains were dried up,
That a fruitful land yielded nothing because of the wickedness of them that dwelt therein;
And, again, he made the dry land full of water, and in the dry land springs of water;
And hath set the hungry to prepare a city to dwell in,
and sow the fields, and plant the vineyards, and reap the fruit thereof year by year;
And he blessed them, and they multiplied almost, and gave them much cattle;
Those who were oppressed and weakened by the evil one who had compelled and pressed upon them,
When contempt was heaped upon the princes, and all things were in error and desolate;
And he protected the poor from misery, and multiplied his seed as a flock.
The righteous shall see and rejoice: and all wickedness shall be shut up.
Who is wise, and keepeth these things? Then shall they know how many benefits the LORD hath bestowed.
a psalm song of David.
God, I am in earnest; I will sing and write, my glory also. Come, psalteries and harps! I will be up early.
I will give thee thanks, O LORD, among the nations; I will sing praise unto thee among the people.
For thy mercy reacheth as far as the heavens, and thy truth as far as the clouds go.
Exalt yourself, O God, above the heavens, and your glory above all the earth,
That thy dear friends may be done. Help with thy right hand, and hear me.
God speaketh in his sanctuary: I am glad, and will divide Shechem, and measure the valley of Shushoth.
Gilead is mine, Manasseh also is mine, and Ephraim is the power of my head; Judah is my prince,
Moab is my washing-pot; I will stretch out my shoe upon Edom; upon the Philistines will I exult.
Who will lead me into a strong city? Who will lead me to Edom?
Wilt thou not do it, O God, which hast cast us off, and wilt thou not go forth, O God, with our host?
give us help in trouble, for the help of men is of no avail.
With God we will do deeds. He will trample under our enemies.
a psalm of David, to be sung. God, my glory, do not be silent!
For they have opened their ungodly and false mouths against me, and have spoken against me with a false tongue.
And they speak evil against me in every place, and fight against me without a cause.
For that I love them, they are against me: but I pray.
they prove me evil for good, and hate for love.
Set the wicked over him; and let Satan stand at his right hand.
Whosoever shall be taught the same, that his life must be ungodly, and his prayer sin.
Let his days be few, and let another receive his office.
His children shall be orphans, and his wife a widow.
His children must go astray, begging and seeking, as those that are corrupt.
Let the usurer suck out all that he hath; and let strangers rob his goods.
And let no man do him good, neither let any man have pity on his fatherless.
His seed must be cut off; their name must be destroyed in the other generation.
Let his father's iniquity be remembered before the LORD, and let not his mother's sin be blotted out.
Let the LORD never take them out of his sight, and let their remembrance be cut off from the earth,
Because he had no mercy at all, but persecuted the wretched, and the poor, and him that was afflicted, to put him to death.
And he would have the curse, and it shall come upon him: but he would not have the blessing, and it shall be far from him.
And he put on the curse like his shirt; and it went into his inward parts like water, and like oil into his bones.
Let it be unto him as a garment to be put on, and as a girdle to be girded withal.
So be it done unto them of the LORD that are against me, and speak evil against my soul.
But thou, O Lord, be thou with me for thy name's sake: for thy mercy is my consolation: save me.
For I am poor and wretched; my heart is slain within me.
I pass away as a shadow that is driven away, and am chased away as the locusts.
My knees are weak from fasting; and my flesh is lean, and hath no fat.
And I must be their mockery: when they see me, they shake their heads.
Help me, O LORD my God; help me according to thy mercy,
That they may know that this is thy hand, that thou, O Lord, doest these things.
If they curse, bless thou. If they set themselves against me, they shall be put to shame: but let thy servant rejoice.
My adversaries must be clothed with shame, and be clothed with their shame as with a garment.
I will give great thanks unto the LORD with my mouth, and will praise him among many;
For he standeth at the right hand of the poor, to save him from them that condemn his life.
A psalm of David. The LORD said unto my LORD, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
The LORD shall send the scepter of thy kingdom out of Zion. Rule among your enemies!
After thy victory thy people shall willingly sacrifice unto thee in holy, adornment. Thy children shall be born unto thee as the dew out of the dawn.
The LORD hath sworn, and will not repent: thou art a priest for ever after the manner of Melchizedech.
The LORD at thy right hand shall smite kings in the time of his wrath.
He shall judge the nations; he shall do great slaughter; he shall bruise the head of great countries.
He shall drink of the brook by the way: therefore shall he lift up his head.
Great are the works of the LORD: he that regardeth them taketh pleasure in them.
That which he hath ordained is praiseworthy and glorious; and his righteousness endureth for ever.
He hath instituted a memorial of his wonders, the gracious and merciful LORD.
He giveth food unto them that fear him: he remembereth his covenant for ever.
He shall declare his mighty works unto his people, that he may give them the inheritance of the heathen.
The works of his hands are truth and judgment; all his commandments are righteous.
They shall be preserved for ever and ever, and shall be done faithfully and honestly.
He sendeth a salvation unto his people: he hath promised that his covenant shall endure for ever. Holy and holy is his name.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: it is a subtle prudence: the praise of him that doeth it endureth for ever.
Hallelujah! Blessed is he that feareth the LORD, that hath great delight in his commandments.
The seed shall be mighty in the earth: the generation of the upright shall be blessed.
Riches and fullness shall be in their house, and their righteousness shall endure for ever.
To the upright there ariseth light in the darkness from him that is gracious, and merciful, and just.
Blessed is he that is merciful, and lendeth willingly, and judgeth his goods, that he do wrong to none.
For he shall abide for ever: the righteous shall never be forgotten.
If a plague come, he feareth not: his heart hopeth in the LORD without fear.
His heart is confident, and fears not, till he see his delight in his enemies.
He scattereth, and giveth to the poor: his righteousness endureth for ever: his horn is exalted with glory.
The wicked shall see it, and be grieved: he shall gnash his teeth, and perish. For what the wicked would have, that is lost.
hallelujah! Praise, ye servants of the LORD, praise the name of the LORD!
Blessed be the name of the LORD from henceforth even for ever.
From the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same be the name of the LORD praised.
The LORD is high above all nations: his glory is as far as the heavens.
Who is like unto the LORD our God? Who hath set himself so high
And look upon the low things in heaven and in earth;
Who raiseth up the lowly out of the dust, and exalteth the poor out of the dung,
To set him beside the princes, beside the princes of his people;
Who maketh the barren to dwell in the house, that she may be a joyful mother of children. Hallelujah!
When Israel came forth out of Egypt, the house of Jacob out of the strange nation,
Judah was his sanctuary, Israel his dominion.
The sea saw, and fled: Jordan turned back;
The mountains skipped like lambs, the hills like young sheep.
What was thine, O sea, that thou fledst? and thou Jordan, that thou turnedst back;
Ye mountains, that ye should leap like lambs; ye hills, like young sheep?
Before the LORD the earth worshippeth, before the God of Jacob,
Who changed the rock into a lake of water, and the stones into fountains of water.
Not unto us, O LORD, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory for thy mercy and truth.

A psalm of David, to be sung. O Lord, thou searchest me, and knowest me.
I sit, or rise up, thou knowest: thou understandest my thoughts afar off.
I walk, or lie down; thou art about me, and seest all my ways.
For, behold, there is not a word upon my tongue, which thou, LORD, knowest not all things.
Thou wilt do what I do before or after, and holdest thine hand over me.
Such knowledge is too strange and too high for me; I cannot understand it.
Whither shall I go before thy spirit, and whither shall I flee before thy face?
If I go to heaven, behold, thou art there. If I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there also.
If I took wings of the dawn, and abode by the uttermost sea,
Yet thine hand shall lead me there, and thy right hand shall hold me.
If I say, Let darkness cover me, the night also shall be light round about me;
For even darkness is not dark with thee, and the night shineth as the day: darkness is as the light.
For thou hast my kidneys in thy power: thou wast over me in my mother's womb.
I thank thee that I am marvellously made: marvellous are thy works, and my soul knoweth them.
My bones were not hid from thee, when I was made in secret, when I was formed in the lower parts of the earth.
Thine eyes saw me when I was yet unprepared, and all the days were written in thy book, which were yet to come, and there was none of them.
But how precious in my sight, O God, are your thoughts! How great is their sum!
If I were to count them, they would be more than the sand. When I wake, I'll still be with you.
O God, that thou wouldest slay the wicked, and that the bloodthirsty would depart from me!
For they speak blasphemy against thee, and thine enemies rise up without a cause.
I hate, O LORD, them that hate thee, and am turned away upon them, that they should set themselves against thee.
I hate them in a right earnestness; therefore they are an enemy unto me.
Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know how I mean;
And see if I be in an evil way, and guide me in an everlasting way.

a psalm of David. O LORD, I cry unto thee; make haste unto me; hear my voice when I call upon thee.
Let my prayer be accepted before thee as an incense, and the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
O LORD, keep my mouth, and keep my lips.
Incline not mine heart unto any evil, to lead an ungodly life with the transgressors, that I eat not of that which is dear unto them.
The righteous smite me kindly, and punish me: it shall do me good as a balm upon my head. For I pray always that they do me no hurt.
Their teachers must be overthrown upon a rock: then shall my doctrine be heard, that it may be sweet.
Our bones are scattered as far as hell, as one that scattereth and scattereth the earth.
For in thee, O Lord, do mine eyes look; I trust in thee: forsake not my soul.
Keep me from the snare which they have laid for me, and from the snare of the workers of iniquity.
The wicked must fall into their own net together, but I always pass by.

a psalm of David. Hear my prayer, O Lord; hear my supplication for thy truth's sake; hear me for thy righteousness' sake.
And enter not into judgment with thy servant: for there is none living that is righteous before thee.
For the enemy pursueth my soul, and destroyeth my life to the ground; he layeth me in darkness, as the dead in the world.
And my spirit is troubled within me; my heart is consumed in my flesh.
I remember the former times; I speak of all thy doings, and tell of the works of thy hands.
I stretch forth my hands unto thee: my soul thirsteth for thee as a dry land. Sela.

Deliver me, O my God, from mine enemies: in thee have I refuge.
Teach me to do according to thy good pleasure: for thou art my God: let thy good spirit lead me in a straight path.
O LORD, quicken me for thy name's sake, bring my soul out of trouble for thy righteousness' sake;

A psalm of David. Blessed be the LORD my stronghold, which teacheth my hands to fight, and my fists to war,
My goodness, and my fortress, my refuge, and my deliverer, my shield, in whom I trust, that compelleth my people under me.
O LORD, what is man, that thou art so mindful of him? and the child of man, that thou hast such regard for him?
Man is as nothing; his time passeth away like a shadow.
O LORD, incline thy heavens, and descend; touch the mountains, and they shall smoke.
Let thy lightning flash, and scatter them: shoot thy beams, and scatter them.
Send thine hand from on high, and deliver me, and deliver me from great waters, from the hand of strange children,
Whose doctrine is not profitable, and their works are false.
God, I will sing unto thee a new song; I will play unto thee upon the psaltery of ten strings.
Who givest victory unto kings, and deliverest thy servant David from the murderous sword of the wicked.
Deliver me also, and deliver me out of the hand of strange children, whose doctrine is not profitable, and whose works are false,
That our sons may grow up in their youth like plants, and our daughters like hewn out oriels, like palaces,
And our storehouses shall be full, which may give out one store after another; and our flocks shall bear a thousand and an hundred thousand in our villages;

Blessed are the people, to whom it is so. But blessed are the people, whose God is the LORD!
praise of David. I will exalt thee, O my God, O king; I will praise thy name for ever and ever.

And I gave my heart to search and search wisely all that is done under heaven. God has given the children of men such unhappy trouble that they have to toil in it.
I looked upon all that is done under the sun, and, behold, it was all vain and pitiful.

And I said in mine heart, Behold, I am become glorious, and have more wisdom than all that were before me in Jerusalem: and my heart hath learned and experienced many things.
And I set my heart to learn wisdom, and folly, and prudence. But I perceived that these things are trouble.
For where there is much wisdom, there is much sorrow: and he that teacheth much, suffereth much.
I said in mine heart, Well, I will live well, and have good days. But, behold, this also was vain.
I spoke to the laughter: You are great and to joy: What are you doing?

Then thought I in mine heart to draw my body from wine, and to draw my heart unto wisdom, to lay hold on that which is foolishness, until I should learn what is good for men to do, as long as they live under heaven.
I did great things; I built houses, I planted vineyards,
I made me gardens and pleasure gardens, and planted therein all manner of fruitful trees;
I made me pools to water the forest of green trees.
I had menservants, and maidservants, and servants; I had a greater substance of oxen and sheep than all that were before me in Jerusalem.
I also gathered me silver, and gold, and treasure of kings and of countries. I made me singers, and singers, and the lust of men, and all manner of strings,
And increased upon all them that were before me in Jerusalem: wisdom also abode with me.
And all things whatsoever mine eyes desired I left them, and withheld no joy from my heart, that it should rejoice in all my labour: and this I counted my portion in all my labour.
And when I had considered all my works that my hand had done, and the labour that I had laboured under, behold, it was all vain and pitiful, and there was nothing left under the sun.
Then turned I to see wisdom, and prudence, and folly. For who knoweth what manner of man he shall be after the king whom they have made ready?
Then I saw that wisdom surpassed folly, as light surpasseth darkness,
That the wise man's eyes are in his head, but fools walk in darkness; and yet he perceiveth that one is like another.
Then thought I in mine heart, Because the fool is like me, why then have I sought wisdom? Then thought I in mine heart, That these things also are vanity.
For the wise man is not remembered for ever, neither is the fool: and the days to come forget all things: and as the wise dieth, so dieth the fool.
Wherefore I was displeased to live: for I was displeased with the things that are done under the sun, that they were so vain and troublesome.
And all my labour that I had under the sun grieved me, that I should leave the same unto a man that should be after me.
For who knoweth whether he shall be wise or foolish? And yet shall reign in all my work, Which I have wisely done under the sun. That also is vain.
Therefore I turned, that my heart might depart from all the work that I have done under the sun.
For a man that hath wrought his work with wisdom, and understanding, and skill, must leave it for an inheritance to another that hath not wrought it. This also is vain, and a great misfortune.
For what shall a man get of all his labour and toil of his heart that he hath under the sun?
For all the days of his life he hath sorrow, and grief, and his heart hath not rested at night? This also is vain.
Is it not better for a man to eat and drink, and for his soul to be in good health in his work? But these things also have I seen, that they are of the hand of God.
For who hath more gladly eaten and rejoiced than I?

For to the man that pleaseth him he giveth wisdom, and understanding, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth calamity, that he may gather and heap, and yet be given to him that pleaseth God. Therefore this also is a vain sorrow.
To every thing there is a season; and to every purpose under heaven there is an hour.

work as you will, so you can't do more.
Therefore I saw the trouble which God gave to men, that they should be afflicted within.
But he doeth all things in his good time, and maketh their hearts to be anxious, how things shall be in the world: for man cannot do the work that God doeth, neither the beginning nor the end.
Therefore I perceived that there was nothing better in it, but to be merry, and to do him good in his life.
For every man that eateth and drinketh, and hath good courage in all his work, is the gift of God.
I perceived that whatsoever God doeth, that continueth for ever: there is nothing to add unto it, neither to take away from it: and this is what God doeth, that men should fear him.
What God doeth, that standeth; and what he will do, that shall come to pass: for he seeketh and pursueeth after him.
Further, I saw under the sun a place of judgment, where was an ungodly creature; and a place of righteousness, where were ungodly men.
Then thought I in mine heart, God must judge the righteous and the wicked: for there is a season to every purpose and to every work.
I have spoken in my heart of the nature of men, wherein God doth indicate and make them look as if they were among themselves as cattle.
For man is as the beast: as the beast dieth, so dieth he; and they have all the same breath: and man hath nothing more than beast: for all are vain.
All things come to one place: all things are made of dust, and return to dust.
Who knoweth whether the breath of men go up, and the breath of cattle go down under the earth?
Therefore I saw that there is nothing better than that a man should be glad in his work: for that is his portion. For who shall bring him to see what shall come after him?
I turned, and saw all that were wronged under the sun: and, behold, there were tears of them that were wronged, and had no comforter: and they that wronged them were too mighty to have a comforter.
Then I praised the dead which were dead, rather than the living which had life.
And he that is not yet is better than both, and is not aware of the evil that is done under the sun.
I have seen work and skill in all things: one envieth another. That also is vain and toil.
For a fool claspeth his fingers together, and eateth his flesh.
It is better to have one hand full of peace than both fists full of trouble and sorrow.
I turned, and saw vanity under the sun.

He is one, and not one; he hath neither child nor brethren: neither is there an end of his labour, neither are his eyes full of riches. Whom do I labour after, and break off my soul? This also is vain, and wicked toil:
Two are better than one: for they enjoy their work well.
If a man fall, his companion shall help him up. Woe to him who is alone! If he falls, there is no one to help him up.
even if two lie together, they warm themselves; how can' one become warm?
One may be overcome, but two may withstand: for a threefold cord is not easily broken.
A poor child that is wise is better than an old king that is a fool, and knoweth not how to beware.
One cometh out of prison unto the kingdom; and one born in his kingdom is impoverished.
And I saw that every living thing that is under the sun walketh by one in the child that shall arise in his stead.
And there was no end of the people that went before him, or of them that followed him: yet they were not glad. This also is a vain and grievous thing.
For where there is much sorrow, there come dreams: and where there are many words, there is heard a fool.
When thou vowest a vow unto God, thou shalt not consume to keep it: for he hath no pleasure in fools. That which thou vowest, keep it.
It is better that thou vow nothing, than that thou keep not that which thou vowest.
Curse not thy mouth, that it may deceive thy flesh: neither say thou before the angel, I am innocent. God will be angry with thy voice, and condemn all the works of thy hands.
Where there are many dreams, there is vanity and many words; but fear God!

When thou seest the poor wronged, and righteousness and justice taken away in the land, marvel not at the noble: for there is yet a high guardian above the high, and there are yet higher than these two.
About this is the king throughout all the land, to build the field.
He that loveth money shall never be satisfied with money: he that loveth riches shall not profit thereby. This also is vain.
For where there is much good, there are many that eat it: and what is he worthy that hath it, without seeing it with his eyes?
To him that worketh sleep is sweet, whether he have eaten little, or whether he have eaten much: but the rich man's abundance maketh him not sleep.
It is an evil plague that I have seen under the sun, to keep wealth to the hurt of him that hath it.
For the rich man perisheth with great sorrow: and if he have begotten a son, he hath nothing left in his hand.
As he came naked from his mother's womb, so he goeth again as he came, and taketh nothing of his work in his hand with him when he goeth.
This is an evil plague, because he is gone as he came. What profit is it to him, that he hath wrought in the wind?
For all his life he hath eaten in darkness, and in great sorrow, and in sickness, and in grief.

Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and come and hear. This is better than the sacrifice of fools: for they know not what evil they do. Chap. 5, v. 1. Be not quick with thy mouth, and let not thy heart haste to speak any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
Now therefore I consider it good to eat and to drink, and to be of good cheer in all the work that a man doeth under the sun all the days of his life, which God giveth him: for that is his portion.
For unto whomsoever God giveth riches, and goods, and power, to eat thereof, and to drink thereof for his portion, and to be merry in his labour, this is the gift of God.
For he thinketh not much of the miserable life, because God delighteth his heart.
It is a calamity that I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men:

One to whom God hath given riches, goods, and honor, and lacketh none that his heart desireth, and yet God giveth him not power to enjoy them, but another devoureth them: this is vain and an evil plague.
If he beget an hundred children, and live so long, that he live many years, and his soul be not satisfied with good, and remain without a grave, of him I say that untimely birth is better than he.
For in vanity he cometh, and in darkness he passeth away, and his name abideth in darkness,
Is not glad of the sun, and knows no rest either here or there.
Though he live two thousand years, yet hath he no good courage. Is it not all in one place?
To every man is laid up work according to his measure: but the heart cannot keep it up.
For what doth a wise man judge more than a fool? What dare Anne, that he should be among the living?
It is better to use the present good, than to think of other things. This is also vanity and misery.
What is the matter, though a man be highly renowned, yet know ye that he is a man, and be not grieved with that which is too mighty for him?
For the vain thing is too much: what hath a man more of it?
For who knoweth what shall profit a man in life, as long as he liveth in his vanity, which passeth away as a shadow? Or who shall tell man what shall come after him under the sun?
a good rumour is better than good ointment, and the day of death neither the day of birth.
It is better to go into the house of complaint than into the house of drunkenness: in the latter is the end of all men, and the living take it to heart.
It is better to mourn than to laugh: for by mourning the heart is made better.
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, and the heart of fools in the house of gladness.
It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than to hear the song of fools.
For the laughter of the fool is as the crackling of thorns among pots; and that also is vain.
A contumacious man maketh a wise man unwilling, and corrupteth a meek heart.
the end of a thing is better than its beginning. A patient spirit is better than a high spirit.
Be not quick to anger: for anger resteth in the heart of a fool.
Say not, What is it that the former days were better than these? For thou askest not wisely.
wisdom is good with an inheritance, and helps that one may rejoice in the sun.
For wisdom shieldeth, and money also shieldeth: but wisdom giveth life to him that hath it.
Behold the works of God: for who can make evil that which he bendeth?
Be of good cheer in the good day, and take the evil day also for good: for this God hath made beside that, that man should not know what is to come.
All manner of things have I seen in the time of my vanity. There is a righteous man that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is an ungodly man that liveth long in his wickedness.
Be not too righteous, nor too wise, lest thou corrupt thyself.
Be not overmuch ungodly, and be not foolish, lest thou die untimely.
It is good for thee to take hold of these things, and not to let those things out of thine hand: for he that feareth God escapeth all these things.
Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men that are in the city. For there is not a man upon the earth that doeth good, and sinneth not.
Neither take to thine heart all that is said, lest thou hear thy servant curse thee.
For thine heart knoweth that thou hast often cursed others also.
All these things have I tried wisely. I thought I would be wise; but she came farther from me.
It is far off; what shall it be? and it is very deep; who shall find it?
I turned my heart to know, and to search, and to seek wisdom and arts; to know the folly of the wicked, and the error of the foolish,
And found that such a woman, whose heart is a net and a snare, and her hands are bands, is more bitter than death. He that pleaseth God shall escape her; but the sinner shall be snared by her.
Behold, these things have I found, saith the preacher, one by one, that I might learn art.
And my soul seeketh yet, and hath not found it. I have found one man in a thousand, but I have not found a woman among them all.
Behold, I have found that God hath made man upright: but they seek many arts. Ch. 8, v. 1. who is so wise? and who can interpret it?
The wisdom of man enlighteneth his face: but he that is bold is hostile,
I keep the word of the King and the oath of God.
Hasten not to depart from his presence, neither tarry in evil: for he doeth that which he lusteth after.
There is power in the king's word: and who shall say unto him, What doest thou?
He that keepeth the commandment shall know no evil: but the heart of a wise man knoweth the time and the manner.
For to every purpose there is a season and a time: for the calamity of man is much with him.
For he knoweth not what hath been; and who shall tell him what shall be?
A man hath not power over the spirit to resist the spirit; neither hath he power in the time of death, neither is he loosed in the battle: neither doth the ungodly deliver the ungodly.
I have seen all these things, and have set my heart upon all the works that are done under the sun. One man at a time ruleth over another to his own hurt.
And there I saw the wicked buried, which had walked, and had walked in the holy place, and were forgotten in the city, because they had done so. This also is vain.
Because judgment of evil works is not soon executed, thereby men's hearts are filled with doing evil.
Though a sinner do evil a hundred times, and yet live long, yet I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, that fear his face.
For it shall not prosper the wicked, neither shall they live long, as a shadow, that fear not God.

There is a vanity that is done in the earth. The righteous are as though they had the works of the wicked; and the wicked are as though they had the works of the righteous. And I said, This also is vanity.

Therefore I commend joy, that there is nothing better for a man under the sun, than to eat and to drink, and to be merry: and such shall he have of the work of his life, which God giveth him under the sun.
I gave my heart to know the wisdom, and to behold the travail that is upon the earth, that no man should see sleep with his eyes day or night.

And I saw all the works of God. For a man cannot find the work that is done under the sun; and the more a man labors to seek, the less he finds. Though he say, I am wise, and know it, yet can he not find it.

For I have taken all these things to heart, to search out all these things, that the righteous and the wise are, and their subjects in the hand of God. But no man knoweth neither the love nor the hate of any that he hath before him.

It befalleth one as well as another, the righteous as well as the wicked, the good and the clean as well as the unclean, he that sacrificeth as well as he that sacrificeth not. As it is with the good, so it is with the sinner. As it is with the perjurer, so it is with him who fears the oath.
For the heart of the wise is on his right hand: but the heart of the fool is on his left.

This is an evil thing of all that is done under the sun, that it goeth to one as it goeth to another: therefore also the heart of men is filled with evil, and folly is in their heart, while they live; and after that they die.
Though the fool himself be foolish in his doings, yet he thinketh every man a fool.
For with all living things there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
Wherefore, if a mighty one go against thy will, be not dismayed: for forbearance stilleth great evil.
For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither do they deserve any more; for their memory is forgotten,
That they be no more loved, nor hated, nor envied; neither have they any more any part in the world in anything that is done under the sun.
Go therefore, eat thy bread with gladness, drink thy wine with good courage: for thy work is pleasing unto God.
Let thy garments be always white, and let not thy head lack ointment.

Use life with thy wife, whom thou lovest, as long as thou hast the vain life which God hath given thee under the sun, as long as thy vain life endureth: for this is thy portion in life, and in thy work which thou doest under the sun.
Whatsoever thou hast power to do, do it fresh: for in hell, whither thou goest, there is neither work, nor skill, nor understanding, nor wisdom.

I turned, and saw how it is under the sun, that to run is not to be swift, to fight is not to be strong, to eat is not to be skillful, to be rich is not to be wise; that a man may be pleasant is not that he may do a thing well, but all depends upon time and fortune.
Neither knoweth man his time: but as the fishes are taken with a noisome snare, and as the birds are caught with a snare, so men are taken with the evil time, when it suddenly cometh upon them.
I have also seen this wisdom under the sun, which seemed great unto me,
And there was a small city, and few people in it: and there came a great king, and filled it, and built great fortresses about it,
And there was found in it a poor wise man, which was able to save that city by his wisdom: and no man remembered that poor man.
Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength. Nor was the poor man's wisdom despised, nor his words obeyed.
For the words of the wise are more effectual among the quiet, than the shouting of lords among fools.
For wisdom is better than armour: but a few knaves destroy much good. Ch. 10, v. 1. So the noxious flies spoil good ointments. Therefore at times folly is better than wisdom and honour.
There is a calamity that I have seen under the sun, namely, foolishness, which is common among the mighty,
That a fool sitteth in great dignity, and the rich sit down here.
I saw servants on horses, and princes walking as servants.
But he that maketh a pit shall fall into three: and he that breaketh the fence shall be stung by a serpent.
He that rolleth away stones shall have trouble; and he that cleaveth wood shall be hurt thereby.
If an iron be blunt, and the edge remain unsharpened, it must be sharpened again with power: so also wisdom followeth diligence.
A launderer is nothing better than a serpent that stings unsworn.
The words of a wise man's mouth are pleasant: but the lips of a fool devour him.
The beginning of his words is foolishness, and the end is pernicious folly.
A fool speaketh much: for a man knoweth not what hath been; and who shall tell him what shall be after him?

(For by slothfulness the beams sink, and by negligent hands the house is dripping).
That maketh bread to make merry, and wine to make glad the living, and money to make all things work for them.
Curse not the king in thine heart, neither curse the rich man in thy bedchamber: for the fowls of the air carry the voice, and they that have wings repeat it.
Let thy bread pass over the waters, and thou shalt find it for a long time.
Divide from among seven, and from among eight: for thou knowest not what evil shall come upon the earth.
When the clouds are full, they give rain upon the earth: and when the tree falleth, let it fall toward the south, or toward the north, upon what place it falleth, there shall it lie.
He that looketh to the wind soweth not, and he that looketh to the clouds reapeth not.
As thou knowest not the way of the wind, and as the bones are prepared in the womb, so thou canst not know the work of God which he doeth everywhere.
Early see thy seed, and let not thine hand depart in the evening: for thou knowest not whether it be this or that: and if it be both, so much the better.
The light is sweet, and it is pleasant to the eyes to see the sun.
If a man live a long time, and be merry in all things, he remembereth but the evil days, that they are so many: for all that he hath met with is vain.

and the doors of the street are shut, that the voice of the miller's wife may be hushed, and awake when the bird sings, and all the daughters of song bend down,

These words of the wise are spears and nails, written by the masters of the assemblies, and given by a shepherd.

I am black, but I am lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the carpets of Solomon.

Look not upon me, because I am black: for the sun hath burned me. My mother's children are angry with me. They have made me the keeper of the vineyards: but the vineyard which I had, I have not kept it.
Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou restest at noonday, that I walk not to and fro among the flocks of thy companions.
If thou knowest not thyself, O fairest of women, go out in the footsteps of the sheep, and feed thy goats by the shepherds' houses.
I will liken thee, my friend, unto my travelling witness unto Pharaoh's chariot.
Thy cheeks are set in braces, and thy neck in chains.
We will make thee clasps of gold, and silver spangles.

My friend is a clump of myrrh that hangeth between my breasts.
My friend is a grape of Kopher unto me in the vineyards of Engeddi.
Behold, my friend, thou art fair, fair art thou; thine eyes are as the eyes of a dove.
Behold, my friend, thou art fair and lovely. Our bed is green.
The beams of our houses are cedars, and our laths are cypresses.
I am a flower to Saron, and a rose in the valley.
As a rose among thorns, so is my friend among daughters.
As an apple tree among the wild trees, so is my friend among the sons. I sit under the shade of him whom I desire, And his fruit is sweet to my throat.
He leadeth me into the wine cellar, and love is his banner over me.
He hath refreshed me with flowers, and fed me with apples: for I am sick of love.
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand is upon me.
I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up my friend, nor stir her up, until ye yourselves fall.
There is the voice of my friend. Behold, he cometh, and leapeth upon the mountains, and leapeth upon the hills.
My friend is like a roe deer, or a young hart. Behold, he standeth behind our wall, and looketh through the window, and peepeth through the lattice.
My friend answereth and saith unto me, Arise, my friend, my fair one, and come hither.
For, behold, the winter is past, and the rain is gone and gone;
The flowers are come forth in the land, the spring is come, and the turtledove is heard in our land;
The fig tree has gained nodes, the vines have gained eyes and give their smell. Arise, my friend, and come, my beautiful one, come here!
My dove in the holes of the rock, in the clefts of the stone, show me thy form, let me hear thy voice. For thy voice is sweet, and thy form lovely.
Fear us the foxes, the little foxes that spoil the vineyards: for our vineyards have gained eyes.
My friend is mine, and I am his that feedeth among the roses,
Till the day be cool, and the shadow depart. Turn back, become like a deer, my friend, or like a young stag on the Scheideberge!
I sought in my bed at night him whom my soul loveth. I sought, but found him not.
I will arise, and go about the city in the streets and lanes, and seek him whom my soul loveth. I sought, but found him not.
The watchmen that go about the city found me: Have ye not seen him whom my soul loveth?
And when I had passed a little before them, I found him whom my soul loveth. I hold him, and will not leave him, Till I bring him into my mother's house, Into my mother's chamber.
I adjure you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes or hinds of the field, that ye stir not up my friend, nor stir her up, till she herself be fallen.
Who is she that cometh up out of the wilderness as a straight smoke, as the smoke of myrrh, and frankincense, and all manner of powder of an apothecary?
Behold, round about the bed of Solomon stand threescore and ten strong men of the mighty men of Israel.
They hold all swords, and are skillful in battle. Every man hath his sword upon his thigh for fear of the night.
And king Solomon made him a litter of wood out of Lebanon.
The pillars thereof were of silver, the covering of gold, the seat of purple, the floor in the midst thereof was beautifully paved for the daughters' sake in Jerusalem.
Come forth, ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon in the crown, that his mother hath crowned him in the day of his marriage, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.
Behold, my friend, thou art fair behold, fair art thou! Thine eyes are as the eyes of doves among thy braids. Thy hair is like the herds of goats that are shorn in mount Gilead.
Thy teeth are like the flock of circumcised wool, which come out of the flood, which bear twins at all times; and there is none barren among them.
Thy lips are like a rosy cord, and thy speech is sweet. Thy cheeks are like the slit on the pomegranate between thy braids.
Thy neck is like the tower of David, built with breastworks; there hang a thousand shields thereon, and all the weapons of the mighty.
thy two breasts are like two young doe twins grazing among the roses,
Till the day be cool, and the shadow be removed. I will go to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
thou art all things fair, my friend, and there is no spot in thee.
Come, my bride, from Lebanon, come from Lebanon. Come in, come in from the height of Amana, from the height of Senir and Hermon, from the dwellings of lions, from the mountains of leopards.
Thou hast taken my heart, my sister, dear bride, with thine eyes one, and with thy necklaces one.
How beautiful are thy breasts, my sister, my dear bride! Thy breasts are more sweet than wine, and the smell of thy ointments surpasses all spices.
Thy lips, my bride, are as honey dripping; honey and milk are under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments is as the smell of Lebanon.
My sister, dear bride, you are a closed garden, a closed spring, a sealed well.
Thy growth is like a garden of pomegranates, with noble fruit, Cyprus with nard,
nard with saffron, calamus, and tin names, with all manner of trees of frankincense, myrrh, and aloes, with all the best spices.
As a garden fountain, as a spring of living waters flowing from Lebanon.
Arise, north wind, and come, south wind, and woe through my garden, that his spices may drip!
I sleep, but my heart waketh. There is the voice of my friend knocking, Open to me, my dear friend, my sister, my dove, my pious: for my head is full of dew, and my locks of night- drops.
I have taken off my skirt, how shall I put it on again? I have washed my feet, how shall I sully them again?
But my friend put his hand through the hole, and my body trembled at it.
And I arose to give up my friend; and my hands were dripping with myrrh, and myrrh ran upon my fingers by the latch of the lock.
And when I had opened my friend, he was gone, and departed. Then went out my soul after his word: I sought him, but found him not: I called, but he answered me not.
And the keepers of the city found me, and smote me sore: the keepers of the wall took away my veil.
I beseech you, ye daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my friend, tell him that I lie sick of love.
What is thy friend above other friends, O thou fairest of women? What is thy friend before other friends, that thou hast thus adjured us?
my friend is white and red, chosen among many thousands.
His head is the finest gold. His curls are frizzy, black as a raven.
His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of water, washed with milk, and standing in fullness.
His cheeks are like the growing of the spices of the apothecaries. His lips are like roses dripping with flowing myrrh.
His hands are like rings of gold, full of turquoises; His body is as pure ivory adorned with sapphires.
His legs are like pillars of marble, founded upon feet of gold. His form is like Lebanon, chosen like cedars.
His throat is sweet, and all sweetness. Such a one is my friend; my friend is such, O daughters of Jerusalem!

Let my friend come into his garden, and eat of his noble fruit. Chap. 5, v. 1. I come, my sister, dear bride, into my garden. I have broken off my myrrh together with my spices; I have eaten of my seed together with my honey; I have drunk of my wine together with my milk. Eat, my beloved, and drink, my friends, and be drunk!
My friend is mine, and I am his that feedeth among the roses.
Thou art fair, my friend, as Thirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, terrible as Heerspitzen.
Turn away thine eyes from me; for they make me ruthless: thy hair is as a flock of goats shorn in mount Gilead.
Thy teeth are as a flock of sheep which come out of the flood, which bear twins every one; and there is not one barren among them.
your cheeks are like a slit on the pomegranate between your braids.
Sixty are the queens, and fourscore the concubines; and there is no number of virgins.
But one is my dove, my pious; one is her mother's beloved, and her mother's elect. When they saw the daughters, they blessed them: the queens and the concubines praised them.
Who is she that cometh forth as the dawn, fair as the moon, chosen as the sun, terrible as the tops of the hosts?
I went down into the garden of nuts, to see the shrubs by the brook, to see whether the vine blossomed, whether the pomegranates were green.
My soul knew it not, that he had set me by the chariot of Ammi-Nadib.
Return again, return again, O Sulamith! Return again, return again, that we may behold thee! What do you see in Sulamith? The round dance at Mahanaim.

Whither then hath thy friend gone, O thou fairest of women? Whither hath thy friend turned? Let us seek him with thee. Ch. 6, v. 1. My friend is gone down to his garden, to the spice garden, to feed among the gardens, and to break the roses.
How beautiful is thy walk in thy shoes, O prince's daughter! Thy loins are like two clasps together, which the master's hand hath made.
Thy navel is like a round cup that never lacketh drink. Thy belly is like a heap of wheat, covered with roses.
Your two breasts are like two young deer twins.
Thy neck is like an ivory tower. Thine eyes are like the pools of Heshbon, at the gate of Bathrabbim. Thy nose is like the tower of Lebanon, which looketh toward Damascus.
Thy head is upon thee like Carmel. The hair of thy head is bound in folds like the purple of the king.
How beautiful and how lovely art thou, O love of lusts!
Thy length is like a palm tree, and thy breasts like grapes.
I said: I must climb the palm tree and take hold of its branches. Let thy breasts be as grapes upon the vine, and thy nose as the smell of apples.
And thy throat like good wine, which is smooth unto my friend, and speaketh of far-off things.
my friend is mine and he sticks up for me too.
Come, my friend, let us go out into the field, and stay in the villages,
That we may arise early unto the vineyards, and see whether the vine be in blossom, and whether the eyes be grown, and whether the pomegranates be put forth: then will I give thee my breasts.
The lilies give off the smell, and at our door are all kinds of noble fruits. My friend, I have kept both this year's and far-off ones for you.
O that I might find thee, my brother, sucking my mother's breasts, out of doors, and kiss thee, that no man should mock me!
I would lead thee, and bring thee into my mother's house, where thou shouldest teach me: and I would water thee with wine made, and with the juice of my pomegranates.
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand is upon me.
I charge you, daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up nor stir up my love, until ye yourselves be pleased.
Who is she that cometh up from the wilderness, and leaneth upon her friend? Under the apple tree I waked thee, When thy mother bare thee, When she that bare thee lay with thee.
Set me as a seal upon thine heart, and as a seal upon thine arm. For love is strong as death, and zeal is firm as hell. Their embers are fiery, and a flame of the LORD,
That even much water may not quench love, nor the rivers drown it. If a man were to give all that is in his house for love, it would be worth nothing.
Our sister is small and has no breasts. What should we do to our sister, if one should address her now?
If it be a wall, let us build silver bulwarks upon it. If it be a door, let us strengthen it with cedar planks.
I am a wall, and my breasts are as towers. There have I been before his eyes, as which finds peace.
Solomon had a vineyard in Baalhamon. And he gave the vineyard to the keepers, that every one might bring a thousand shekels of silver for the fruit thereof.
My vineyard is before me. To thee, Solomon, is due a thousand; but to the keepers, two hundred, with its fruit.
Thou that dwellest in the gardens, let me hear thy voice: the companies take heed.
Flee, my friend, and be like a deer or young stag on the Würzberge.
This is the vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw of Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Jehizkiah, kings of Judah.
Hear, ye heavens, and earth, take heed. For the LORD speaketh: I have raised up and exalted children, and they have fallen away from me.
An ox knoweth his master, and an ass his master's crib: but Israel knoweth it not, neither do my people hear it.
O woe unto the sinful people, the people of great iniquity, the wicked seed, the children of iniquity, which forsake the LORD, blaspheming the Holy One in Israel, draw back!
What more shall they smite upon you, if ye do but the more to depart? The whole head is sick, the whole heart is dull.
From the sole of his foot even to his head there is no soundness in him, but sores and welts and boils, which are not healed, neither bound up, nor soothed with oil.
Your land is desolate, your cities are burned with fire; strangers devour your fields before your eyes, and is desolate, as that which is devastated by strangers.
And that which is left of the daughter of Zion is as a little house in the vineyard, as a tent of the night in the gourds, as a desolate city.
If the LORD of hosts left us not a little, we should be as Sodom, and as Gomorrha.
Hear the word of the LORD, ye princes of Sodom; give ear to the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrha.

What is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the LORD. I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and of the fat of the fatlings; and I have no desire for the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of goats.
When the protection shall be like ashes, and his doings like sparks, and both shall be kindled together, that no man put them out.
When ye come in to appear before me, who shall require this of your hands, that ye should tread in my court?
Offer no more meat offerings in vain. The incense is abomination unto me: the new moons and the sabbaths, when ye come together, and are troubled and afraid, them will I not like.
My soul hateth your new moons and your seasons: I am weary of them; I am weary of suffering.
And though ye spread forth your hands, yet will I hide mine eyes from you; and though ye pray much, yet will I not hear you; for dear hands are full of blood.
Wash, cleanse yourselves, put away your evil from mine eyes, depart from evil.
Learn to do good, seek justice, help the oppressed, give justice to the fatherless, and help the widow's cause.
Come then, and let us reason together, saith the LORD. If sin be as scarlet, it shall be as white as snow: and if it be as raisin, it shall be as wool.
If ye will obey me, ye shall enjoy the good of the land.
But if ye refuse and disobey, ye shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of the LORD saith it.
How is it that the good city is become a harlot? It was full of justice, righteousness dwelt therein, but now murderers
Thy silver is become foam, and thy drink is mixed with water.
Thy princes are renegades and thieves: they all take gifts gladly, and seek after gifts: they do not do justice to the fatherless, and the widow's cause cometh not before them.
Therefore saith the LORD of hosts, the mighty one in Israel; O woe! I will be comforted by mine enemies, and avenged by mine enemies;
And I will turn mine hand against thee, and sweep away thy foam most purely, and put away all thy tin.
And give thee judges again, as they were before, and councillors, as at the beginning. Then shalt thou be called a city of righteousness, and a pious city.
Zion must be redeemed by judgment, and her captives by righteousness,
That transgressors and sinners should be broken in pieces together, and that they which forsake the LORD should perish.
For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye delight in, and ashamed of the gardens which ye choose,
When ye shall be as an oak tree with dry leaves, and as a garden without water;
This is it that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw of Judah and Jerusalem:
In the latter days the mountain where the house of the LORD is shall surely be higher than all mountains, and shall be exalted above all hills: and all nations shall run unto it,

And many nations shall go and say, Come, and let us go up into the mount of the LORD, unto the house of the God of Jacob, that he may teach us his ways, and that we may walk in his paths. For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD out of Jerusalem.

And he shall judge the nations, and punish many people. And they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. For no nation shall lift up a sword against another, neither shall they learn to fight any more.
Come ye therefore from the house of Jacob, and let us walk in the light of the LORD.
But thou hast forsaken thy people, the house of Jacob: for they do more than they that are against the east, and are as the Philistines, and do much with strange children.
Their land is full of silver and gold, and there is no end of their treasures: their land is full of horses, and there is no end of their chariots.
Their land also is full of idols, and they worship the work of their hands, which their fingers have made.
there the riffraff stoopeth, there the nobles humble themselves. You will not forgive them.
Go into the rock, and hide thyself in the earth, from the fear of the LORD, and from his glorious majesty.
For every high eye shall be abased, and every high man shall stoop: but the LORD alone shall be high in that day.
For the day of the LORD of hosts shall pass upon all that is proud, and upon all that is high, and upon all that is exalted, and shall be humbled,
And over all the tall and lofty cedars of Lebanon, and over all the oaks of Bashan,
Over all the high mountains, and over all the lofty hills,
Over all high towers, and over all strong walls,
Over all the ships in the sea, and over all the delicious work,
That all the high places of men should bow down, and humble themselves which are high; and that the LORD alone should be high at that time.
And the idols shall be utterly destroyed.
And they shall walk in the caves of the rocks, and in the clefts of the earth, for the fear of the LORD, and for his glorious majesty, when he shall arise to terrify the earth.
In that day shall every man cast away his idols of silver and of gold, which he had made for him to worship, into the holes of moles and bats,
That he may grovel in the clefts of the stones and in the crags for the fear of the LORD, and for his glorious majesty, when he shall arise to terrify the earth.
Cease therefore from the man that hath breath in his nostrils: for ye know not how highly he is esteemed.
For, behold, the LORD of hosts shall take from Jerusalem and from Judah every store, all the store of bread, and all the store of water,
